title: STO-54 says nothing about a crash inside the restore procedure; a plain restart after one is the naive boot
description: Found while modelling pv-vwe.11 (Provisiond.Restore). STO-54 orders steps (1)-(3) and OPS-15 quarantines the irreversible queued kinds 'on a restore', but nothing in the set says how the engine knows a store is restored. If the process dies after the restore lands and before step (2)'s pass commits, the successor comes up under STO-5's restart rule on the restored store: OPS-15 inspects running rows only, the executed create is claimed again, and every destructive witness ADR-0023 lists fires. The model refuses to carry a crash as a recovery event for this reason (see the module docstring's omissions). Candidate fix: the restore procedure writes a durable 'restore in progress' row before the startup lock, and OPS-15's pass branches on that row rather than on the operator's knowledge; the row is cleared when step (3) completes. Decide the owner (STO-54 vs OPS-15) and land the sentence, then extend Provisiond.Restore with a crash event and prove the theorems survive it.
close_reason: Rule landed on STO-54 with STO-56's record; Provisiond.Restore carries the crash; gates green

comments.author: master
comments.text:
Specification-ambiguity analysis from a Manager-seat test of gpt-6-astra (2026-09-20, not a real rloop Run — rloop cannot drive a codex Manager today). It picked this ticket off the ready frontier in id order, ran the gates, and blocked rather than choosing a reading, which is what RUN-19 asks for.

The two readings it names:
1. The latest process event determines the boot mode. After the restore lands, the recovery process dies before quarantine commits; its successor is an ordinary restart on the same committed store, so a create restored to queued can be claimed again even if the provider already executed it, and a suspension parent resumes with no operator.
2. The unfinished recovery incident determines the boot mode. A crash does not end the restore incident; successors keep its restrictions until the recovery work is finished. This needs a durable 'restore in progress' distinction the text does not provide.

Passages it cites: STO-5 (05-persistence.md:70) 'A restore from backup is not a restart and is not covered by this sentence'; STO-54's step (2) and its freeze-lift clause (05-persistence.md:1144); OPS-15's restore branch and its 'on a restart; after a restore it waits' suspension exception (03-operation-lifecycle.md:315); and Restore.lean's own omission note, which already points here.

Its recommendation: adopt reading 2 explicitly, with STO-54 owning the incident's lifetime and crash-survival obligations and OPS-15 citing that owner; require the unfinished incident to be durably recognizable before any restored component starts; and say how a repeated step avoids moving the restore instant or repeating credential generation and derivation-index changes. ADR-0023 explains the naive-boot danger but does not settle the interrupted-procedure boundary.

This is the owner's call, not an implementer's: it changes what the system is allowed to do.

comments.author: master
comments.text:
Landed 2026-09-20. Owner: STO-54, per reading 2 of the comment above. STO-56 is the new artifact — `restore_incidents` (`restore_instant`, `steps_completed`, `closed_at`), one open row at a time, written into the restored store before either component starts and closed by the operator. OPS-15 cites STO-54's sentence for its branch instead of carrying a copy; the worker algorithm's startup block reads the record and passes it to the pass.

Departure from this ticket's candidate fix, which said the row 'is cleared when step (3) completes': it is not. Two obligations outlive step (3) — OPS-32's second pass and the operator confirming every waiting parent — and clearing at (3) hands both to a successor that no longer knows it is in an incident. The record instead carries a per-step mark, and the operator closes it when the last obligation is discharged. The marks also answer astra's third point: a marked step does not run again, so the grace is written once, the generation bumped once and the derivation index skipped once; only a step interrupted before its mark repeats, and that repeat is safe on each of its writes (the instant comes from the record, the quarantine is guarded on (id, status = queued), step (3)'s two writes only rise).

The marks were not in the first draft. A two-axis review found what the instant-only record costs: repeating a completed step (1) backdates an `exhausted_since` that a later re-derivation had set, burning the interval LDG-16 exists to give, and pauses the listener a second time for a customer already served. ADR-0023 carries that as the reason the record is not a single bit.

Formal: Provisiond.Restore gains Store.record, Event.crash, afterCrash/faultAfterCrash and the recordDecidesBoot parameter; all five restore theorems now quantify over runs containing crashes, and restart_never_reorders gained the hypothesis that the record is closed — that hypothesis is the finding. Witnesses: crash_inside_procedure_continues_it (the successor keeps the restore mode and serves nothing), crash_inside_procedure_is_the_naive_boot (with the parameter off, the executed create is ordered twice), marked_step_does_not_repeat. ci.yml gains the control row, 37 -> 38; all five Restore controls verified locally, one targeted red each. check-all.sh green unpiped.

title: OPS-45's second marker: 'null where begin rescue was never dispatched' is false between the arming write and the dispatch
description: Found while modelling pv-vwe.7 (Provisiond.Rescue). OPS-45 defines rescue_exited_cleanly three-valued: 'null where begin rescue was never dispatched; false, written before begin rescue (PRV-15) is dispatched'. The two clauses cannot both be read as definitions: a process that dies after the arming write commits and before the dispatch leaves false with no session opened, so null is not equivalent to 'never dispatched'. The model proves the safe direction only, which is the sentence the same paragraph ends on -- 'Null is the only value that means no session was opened' (Provisiond.Rescue.Install.none_means_no_session) -- and records the gap in the module docstring's omissions. This is the same conservatism the first marker carries, and OPS-45 stated it there in the 2026-09-15 rewording: the marker 'establishes that preservation is no longer proven, not that a byte landed', and 'a process that dies between the write and the phase leaves a set marker over an untouched disk'. Candidate fix: reword the null clause the way the first marker's was, so the column's meaning is stated as what it forecloses rather than as a biconditional -- null means no session is known to have been opened, and the pre-dispatch false is the conservative case. No behaviour changes; the classifier already reads false as not-clean. Decide whether OPS-45 or 05-persistence.md's rescue_exited_cleanly row carries the wording (OPS-45 owns the rule) and land it.
close_reason: Amendment landed; Round 2 panel unanimously clean, gates green

title: The citation gate's oldest negative control asserts only a nonzero exit
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`).

## The gap

`.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s "Prove the citation gate can fail" appends a synthetic `OVR-1` quote to
`00-overview.md` and asserts only that `python3 tools/check_citations.py` does not exit zero. It
greps nothing. Its three siblings — "Prove the identifier gate refuses a tiered conformance item",
"Prove the citation gate rejects a declaration name the index does not carry" and "Prove the citation
gate rejects a misquote in a Lean docstring" — each assert the gate's own named message, so a red for
an unrelated reason cannot be mistaken for the planted one.

`pv-vwe.18` gave the gate one more way to exit nonzero before the quote check runs: `main()` now calls
`check_docstrings()` first, and a failed extractor case returns before `load()`. A control that reads
only the exit status can now pass on a failure that has nothing to do with quoted attributions.

Nothing is hidden today: "Run all gates" runs earlier in the same job and would already be red. The
control is weaker than its siblings, not broken.

## Shape

Add `grep -q 'attributes to OVR-1 a phrase OVR-1 does not contain'` on the gate's captured output, the
way the sibling steps do, redirecting to a log first.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The step asserts the gate's named message, not only a nonzero exit
- [ ] Rehearsed by hand on a throwaway copy: the mutation lands, the gate exits 1, the grep matches
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green
close_reason: Implemented the intended diagnostic assertion and verified the negative control.

title: QUOTED: alternative occurrences can lend incompatible delimiter evidence (R7/R8 of pv-muf)
description: Residue of pv-muf, stopped after Round 4. The Round-3 checker (c23c2d2) unions all candidate occurrences of every elision fragment before corresponding_roles(), so alternatives can jointly supply evidence no single selection has. Verified cases (Run 20261005T174914, task.md 'R7-R8 preservation cases'): R7a and R8 accept a corrupted quote (a check's ability to fail); R7b/R7c reject a valid one (loud). Round 4 fixed them with an exhaustive itertools.product over occurrences, which went exponential on realistic quotes (39 s on one LDG-57 probe) and was reverted. A fix needs a joint search that prunes per fragment and stays linear-ish in occurrences; the Round-5 brief (R9) in that Run directory states the cases and timing probes. All inputs found so far are synthetic nested-delimiter text; no current corpus quote is affected. Not for an unattended Sequence: design the search first.

title: The rate is a window median (ADR-0027): one observation cannot move it outside the others
description:
## Problem Statement

`ADR-0027` (2026-09-23) replaces the rate confirmation reference with a window median: the rate
is the lower median of the rate observations accepted inside a deployment-stated window, so one
observation cannot move it outside the range the others carry, and the promise that "a transient
bad reading can move a date but cannot destroy a disk" is kept by construction rather than by
gating actions downstream of the price. The ADR records the three findings that forced it — the
promise stopped at the routing decision, `PRV-13e` still promised the same thing in a unit
`ADR-0026` had retired, and `LDG-16` contradicted itself about what the worker reads — and what
was rejected.

This epic lands the decision in the requirements and then in the formal layer, in that order, as
`pv-vwe.14` and `pv-vwe.20` did for `ADR-0026`. It deletes more than it adds: the reference is
named in eight files and most of `pv-vwe.20`'s setter model goes with it.

## Tickets

Two, in dependency order. The requirements first, because the formal layer models what the text
says (`ADR-0025`); then the formal layer, which also absorbs what remains of `pv-vwe.22`.

## Definition of done

`ADR-0027`'s Consequences section is true of the tree: every rule it names says what the ADR says
it says, `rate_confirmation_ref` appears nowhere outside history and the ADRs that record it, the
median theorem is the tagged home of `LDG-16`'s promise, and `nix develop --command bash
tools/check-all.sh` is green unpiped with one `ci.yml` row per surviving parameter.

title: ADR-0027 in the requirements: the window, the withdrawn reference, PRV-13e restated, LDG-16's worker sentences
description:
## Parent

`pv-gip` — the window median (`ADR-0027`). This ticket lands the decision in the requirements;
`pv-gip.2` then models what the text says (`ADR-0025`), so wording here is load-bearing. The
ADR's Consequences section is the edit list; this ticket names the same edits and no others.

## What to land

Each bullet names the owner of a rule; everywhere else points at it (`AGENTS.md`). Every sentence
that asserts what another requirement says carries that requirement's words.

- **`LDG-58`** states the rate: the lower median of the rate observations whose `observed_at` lies
  inside the last window-length before now; the window's length stated per deployment and per
  billing currency, twenty-four hours by default. It keeps "The rate MUST be the median of at least
  three independent sources." as the rule for one pass's observation, and says that "The count
  MUST be odd, so the median is an observed price rather than an average of two." is a rule about
  the pass's sources: the window's count is whatever the passes produced, and the same principle
  picks the lower of two middle values.
- **`LDG-59`** states three things beside its existing text: its staleness bound also applies to
  the window's newest observation — none inside the bound is **no rate**; fewer than three
  observations inside the window is **no rate**; and a deployment MUST state its window and its
  pass cadence so that a full window holds at least three passes. "Falling back to the last known
  rate MUST NOT happen." stands verbatim, followed by one clause saying the window is not a
  fallback: it is the estimator, and a dead feed still halts. `LDG-40`'s matrix is unchanged; these
  are new inputs to it.
- **`LDG-16`** loses the reference: the arming rule, the discharge rule, "A backward move never
  confirms itself", the reference half of the routing predicate. It keeps the destruction deadline
  and its wall-clock rule, the two bypasses, and the wind-down argument for routing natural expiry
  at once. Its promise is restated to what the window gives — a transient bad reading cannot move
  the rate to a price no honest pass in the window accepted, and cannot destroy a disk that no such
  price would destroy — with the ADR's own sentence about the machine within one honest step. Its
  three worker sentences — "reads neither fact except to clear them", "Neither reaches the
  predicate above", "Both do respect the destruction deadline" — are rewritten so that the set
  contains no sentence saying the worker reads neither fact: the worker's provider call reads the
  deadline and nothing else. The routing predicate becomes: stored `runway_until` past and
  `destroy_not_before` null or past.
- **`PRV-13e`**: "**It MUST also maintain `machines.rate_confirmation_ref` on the terms `LDG-16`
  sets**" (`02-provider-contract.md:297`) goes. "A deficiency MUST persist across more than one
  derivation" is restated in the ADR's two halves — no single observation moves the rate outside
  what the other observations carry, and a rate no honest pass produced needs at least half the
  window to carry it — and the note calling the derivation-count form "the control that matters"
  is retired with a dated note. Its interval-bound paragraph (`:333-337`) currently calls the
  re-derivation interval's ceiling "`LDG-16`'s window"; it is rewritten to say the interval, which
  stays hourly by default, and the rate window, which is `LDG-58`'s, are two different spans, and
  which one "MUST stay small against a machine's runway". Its line at `:322` attributing the
  persistence sentence to `LDG-16` follows the restatement.
- **`LDG-41`**: "`LDG-16`'s **multi-derivation persistence rule** is a security control, not
  smoothing" becomes: `LDG-58`'s window median is that security control — a rolling median is a
  filter, and what the sentence means is that it is not a pricing convenience.
- **`LDG-62`** and **`OPS-41`** say "clears the deadline" where they say "clears both facts"
  (`12-billing-and-ledger.md:1499`, `03-operation-lifecycle.md:702`); their own semantics do not
  change.
- **`LDG-64`**: "close the absorbed window at the first valid rate observation — … by the
  observation that restores `LDG-59`'s quorum" is keyed to the window producing a rate again,
  since after a long outage one observation restores quorum and no rate.
- **`LDG-65`** loses "unless its `rate_confirmation_ref` is armed" and the paragraph explaining
  why "The input that would discharge the reference is the same input whose absence triggers that
  cancellation"; the bound proceeds and respects the deadline, like everything else.
- **`05-persistence.md`**: the machines table loses the `rate_confirmation_ref` row and the
  `destroy_not_before` row's "preserving any `rate_confirmation_ref` already present; cleared by the
  same two writes as the reference". **`STO-49`** gains a retention floor of one window per
  currency beside "retained at least until every subject **with an open increment** has closed one
  past its `observed_at`", loses "**and for as long as any machine's `rate_confirmation_ref` names
  it**", and loses the `acceptance_order` rationale's sentence that the confirmation "is the one
  comparison standing between a poisoned price and a destroyed disk" (`:598-599`); the column and
  its uniqueness stay. **`STO-54`** loses "any `rate_confirmation_ref` already present is
  preserved" and its dated note; the grace, its formula and its steps do not change.
- **`CNF-99`** exchanges its confirmation cases for four window cases: one poisoned pass among
  honest ones moves the rate at most one honest step; a print carried by half the window moves it
  there; a window with no fresh observation is no rate; a thin window is no rate. The restore-grace
  and natural-expiry cases stand.
- **`10-conformance-checklist.md`**'s rate section, "Past the persistence rule (`LDG-16`)", points
  at the window median (`LDG-58`).
- **The wind-down worked example** in `12-billing-and-ledger.md`, if it quotes a rate at one
  instant, says which window produced it.
- **`CONTEXT.md`**'s **Rate** and **Window** entries cite `LDG-58` and `LDG-59` beside `ADR-0027`
  once those rules carry the text.

## Must not touch

`STO-54`'s grace, its formula and its steps — only the reference-preservation clause named above
goes. `LDG-64`'s bound itself. The meter's cadence split (`12-billing-and-ledger.md` around line
745). `LDG-40`'s matrix. `LDG-33`'s formula — "at the current rate" now means the window's median
and the sentence needs no edit.

## The record

`rate_confirmation_ref` is withdrawn, not deleted from history: README's *Requirement conventions*
say how a withdrawn column and its dated notes are kept. Every count cites its list.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `grep -n "rate_confirmation_ref\|persistence rule\|persistence window\|multi-derivation" *.md` finds only dated withdrawal notes (root `*.md`; the ADRs keep their record)
- [ ] For each bullet above, the rule's new sentence is quoted in this ticket's closing comment
      beside the bullet it lands, and `tools/check_citations.py` is green on it
- [ ] `grep -n "reads neither fact" *.md` is empty
- [ ] `STO-49` carries the one-window retention floor
- [ ] `CNF-99` carries the four window cases
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, unpiped
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes, then one panel pass asking
      only whether the rules, the examples, `CNF-99` and `ADR-0027` agree with each other
close_reason: Landed; see closing comment

comments.author: master
comments.text:
pv-gip.1 implemented (uncommitted, for the Manager to judge). Gate `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh`, run unpiped: green at cdadd62 before starting, and green on the final tree:

```
  PASS  formal       (Lean build, axiom policy, @[req] index, regions)
  PASS  identifiers  (append-only, dangling, gaps, ADR refs)
  PASS  fixtures     (WIR-37 JSON, WIR-1a, mermaid structure)
  PASS  obligations  (a duty assigned to another requirement)
  PASS  coverage     (requirements exercised by CNF items)
  PASS  citations    (a claim about what another requirement says; Provisiond.* names)
  PASS  regions      (a marked region is what its declaration emits)
All gates passed.
```

Greps: every root `*.md` hit for `rate_confirmation_ref|persistence rule|persistence window|persistence delay|multi-derivation` is in a dated withdrawal note (02:299, 02:365, 05:267, 12:1589). `reads neither fact` finds nothing. `strictly later|second opinion|both facts|two facts|exhaustion facts` finds only the two dated notes (02:300, 12:1590) and 02:429, whose "two facts" is about a resource release.

## Each bullet, with the new sentence

- **LDG-58**: "The rate is the lower median of the rate observations for its currency — `STO-49`'s rows, one per pass — whose `observed_at` lies inside the last window-length before now: the middle value of those observations in price order, or the lower of the two middle values where their count is even. The window's length is stated per deployment and per billing currency, twenty-four hours by default, with the other deployment parameters (`OVR-19`). The odd-count rule above is about the pass's sources. The window's count is whatever the passes produced, and the same principle picks the lower of two middle values, so the rate is always a price some pass accepted." The first sentence and the odd-count sentence are unchanged, and the new text opens with "That is the rule for one pass's rate observation".
- **LDG-59**: after the unchanged "Falling back to the last known rate MUST NOT happen." comes "`LDG-58`'s window is not a fallback: it is the estimator, and a dead feed still halts." The new text continues: "`LDG-40`'s matrix is unchanged; these are new inputs to it." / "The staleness bound also applies to the window's newest observation — newest by `observed_at`, not by acceptance order, which can disagree with it (`STO-49`). Where none lies inside the bound there is no rate." / "Fewer than three observations inside the window is no rate, because a median of one is that one." / "A deployment MUST state its window and its pass cadence so that a full window holds at least three passes, so the thin case is always an outage and never a configuration."
- **LDG-16**:
  - Promise: "A transient bad reading moves the rate (`LDG-58`) no further than to a neighbouring price some honest pass in the window accepted, and so cannot destroy a disk that no such price would destroy. It promises no more than that. A machine within one honest step of exhaustion can be pushed over by that step, and a plausible price carried by half the window can move the rate to itself; no median refuses either."
  - Predicate: "The exhaustion sweep MUST route a machine where its stored `runway_until` has passed and its `destroy_not_before` is null or past — and MUST NOT route it otherwise."
  - Worker: "`OPS-41` says the worker MUST "re-read that machine's commitment and its `runway_until`" — and its no-mutation abort is one of the two writes above. The worker's provider call reads the deadline and nothing else of this requirement's: an exposure-reducing cancellation MUST NOT make its provider call while its machine's `destroy_not_before` is in the future, whichever path reached the worker."
  - Bypasses: "Two cancellations reach the worker without passing through that predicate". Both quotes (`LDG-64`, `OPS-41`) are unchanged.
  - Deadline: "An authorized future-date write clears the deadline"; "wall clock, and no observation discharges it" is unchanged.
  - The trap paragraph is now a dated note: "Withdrawn 2026-09-23 (`ADR-0027`): the rate confirmation reference, … `ADR-0027` holds that trace and the repairs it refused; `ADR-0026` holds the mark's single-column predecessor…"
  - "still covers wind-down **at the current rate**" is kept verbatim for `LDG-33`.
- **PRV-13e**:
  - The duty to maintain the reference is gone. The history paragraph is now headed "Withdrawn 2026-09-23 (`ADR-0027`): the duty to maintain `machines.rate_confirmation_ref` … the reference itself is withdrawn, and what follows is the record of the forms its setter took."
  - The rule is restated: "No single rate observation moves the rate outside what the window's other observations carry, and a rate outside the range of prices honest passes produced needs at least half the window to carry it — both consequences of the rate being `LDG-58`'s lower median over its window, and `LDG-16` owns the promise they keep."
  - Interval: "the interval MUST stay small against a machine's runway … The interval is not the rate window. The window is `LDG-58`'s, twenty-four hours by default, and is the span the rate is taken over; the interval, hourly by default, is how stale `runway_until` may be."
  - Notes: ":322" now reads "withdrawn from `LDG-16` 2026-09-21 and retired here 2026-09-23". ":328" reads "priced the derivation-count wait, retired 2026-09-23". The "control that matters" note reads "is retired 2026-09-23 (`ADR-0027`)".
- **LDG-41**: "so `LDG-58`'s window median is a security control, not a pricing convenience: a rolling median is a filter, and it is there for the reading it filters out."
- **LDG-62**: "clear the deadline — `LDG-16`'s `machines.destroy_not_before`". **OPS-41**: "clear the deadline — `LDG-16`'s `machines.destroy_not_before`". The historical mention at 03:~719 is left alone.
- **LDG-64**: "close the absorbed window at the observation with which `LDG-58`'s window produces a rate again … The observation that restores `LDG-59`'s quorum is not always that one: after an outage longer than the window it leaves a window too thin to produce a rate". The bound is unchanged.
- **LDG-65**: "A machine whose runway expires mid-outage is cancelled normally, and so is a machine that reaches `LDG-64`'s bound; each respects `LDG-16`'s destruction deadline, like every other exposure-reducing cancellation. What is suspended is *pricing*, not *protection*."
- **05 machines table**: the `rate_confirmation_ref` row is gone. `destroy_not_before` now reads "cleared by an extension (`LDG-62`) and by `OPS-41`'s no-mutation abort", and its italic now reads "With `rate_confirmation_ref`, withdrawn 2026-09-23 (`ADR-0027`), it replaced `exhausted_since`…".
- **STO-49**:
  - Retention floor: "and never less than one window per currency: no row is pruned while its `observed_at` lies inside its currency's window (`LDG-58`)".
  - The reference clause and the "one comparison standing between a poisoned price and a destroyed disk" sentence are gone.
  - The column, its definition and both unique constraints stay. The confirmation use is marked "withdrawn 2026-09-23 (`ADR-0027`)".
- **STO-54**: the preservation clause and its 2026-09-21 note are gone. The grace, formula and steps are unchanged.
- **CNF-99**:
  - Headline: "One adverse rate observation moves the rate no further than to a neighbouring price an honest pass in the window accepted, and a window that cannot produce a rate halts instead of pricing."
  - The four cases: one poisoned pass among five honest ones leaves the rate at the honest rate or one honest step below; a print carried by half a four-observation window becomes the rate; a window with no fresh observation is no rate; a thin window is no rate.
  - The natural-expiry and restore-grace cases stand. The restore case now says "grace" where it said "window".
  - Citations are now `(PRV-13e, LDG-16, LDG-58, LDG-59, STO-49)`.
- **10:615**: "Past the window median (`LDG-58`), a wrong rate is the only external input…"
- **Wind-down worked example**: none found. The only example quoting a rate is the Lean-rendered `ldg38Examples` region (a usage rate, 7 sat/h), which was not touched. The `executive-summary.md` ledger example quotes no satoshi rate.
- **CONTEXT.md**: Rate cites `(LDG-58, ADR-0027)`. Window cites `(LDG-58, ADR-0027)` and "is no rate (`LDG-59`)".
- **Manager's two attributions**: 12:266 now reads "reachable through the wind-down window and a resolved-observed setup fee…". 12:789 now reads "reachable through the wind-down window (`LDG-31`)".

## Edits beyond the list (judge them)

- **`OVR-19` register**: two new rows, "Rate window, per billing currency" (`LDG-58`, `LDG-59`) and "Rate pass cadence" (`LDG-59`). `OVR-19` says "A parameter is on this register or it is not a parameter", and `LDG-59` now says a deployment MUST state both.
- **`STO-49`**: "One row per rate the deployment accepts (`LDG-58`'s median)" now reads "One row per rate observation the deployment accepts (`LDG-58`'s median of one pass's sources)". Under the amended `LDG-58`, a row is an observation, not the rate.
- **`PRV-13e`**: "short enough that all four of those hold" now reads "none of those still standing breaks". Two of the four bullets are now dated history.

## Where the text departs from the ADR's words, and why

The ADR's "cannot move the rate to a price no honest pass in the window accepted" and "a rate that no honest pass produced needs at least half the window to carry it" are both false for a lower median. Counterexample: honest 100/103/104, then replace 103 with a poisoned 101.5. The window becomes 100/101.5/104, and the rate is 101.5, carried by one observation of three. A fresh reader brute-forced windows of 3 to 8 observations and confirmed this. title: LDG-59's two no-rate clocks: staleness continuous, thinness at the pass; the quorum residue in LDG-64 and STO-54
description:
## Parent

`pv-gip` — the window median (`ADR-0027`). Opened by `pv-gip.3`'s Run as a question for the owner;
decided 2026-09-23 and recorded in `ADR-0027`'s freshness bullet. Absorbs `pv-gip.13` (the same
family: residue of the withdrawn per-pass quorum frame).

## Decided

`LDG-59`'s two no-rate conditions are tested on different clocks:

- **Staleness is continuous.** The window's newest observation older than the staleness bound is
  **no rate** at that instant, whether or not a pass has run — a feed that falls silent halts
  between passes rather than holding its last rate. This is what "a dead feed still halts" means;
  `LDG-58`'s "holds until the next such pass" holds only while the window yields a rate.
- **Thinness is tested at the pass.** "Fewer than three observations" is judged by the pass that
  computes the rate, over the window as of that pass. At the minimum window of three passes the
  oldest observation ages out just before each new one arrives; a continuous count would drop the
  rate between passes in steady state, which nobody wants and the text nowhere requires.

## What to land

- **`LDG-59`** (`12-billing-and-ledger.md`, the no-rate paragraph, about `:1098-1122`): one
  sentence for each clock, stated as above, with a dated 2026-09-23 note. The current wording lets
  "holds until the next such pass" (`LDG-58:1081`) be read as pass-gating staleness; close that.
- **`LDG-64`** (`:1152`): "The observation that restores `LDG-59`'s quorum is not always that one"
  — quorum is now a per-pass acceptance test, not a state an observation restores. Reword to the
  window producing a rate, as the clause at `:1146` already does; dated note.
- **`STO-54` step (1)** (`05-persistence.md:1200-1201`, from `pv-gip.13`): "the rate quorum are
  re-established, since `LDG-16` and `STO-36` route on them" — neither reads a quorum (`STO-36`
  routes on `STO-47` status, `LDG-16` on dates). Reword or delete the clause; dated note if it
  carried a trap, otherwise delete outright per README's conventions.
- **`CNF-99`** or `LDG-59`'s items: two cases — at a window of exactly three passes in steady state
  the rate never drops between passes; a feed silent for longer than the staleness bound is no rate
  before any pass runs.

## Must not touch

`LDG-38`; `LDG-58`'s compute-at-pass sentence (it is right; the clarification is `LDG-59`'s);
`tools/`; `docs/adr/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `LDG-59` states both clocks; `grep -n "restores .LDG-59..s quorum" *.md` is empty
- [ ] `STO-54` step (1) no longer says routing reads a quorum
- [ ] The two conformance cases exist
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, unpiped
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes

title: The exhaustion sweep's population is its runway index, so OPS-48's funded-close on a stalled episode may be unreachable
description:
## Parent

`pv-gip`. Found by the 2026-09-23 panel on the inherited-fence question (`claude-opus-5`), verified
against the schema. **Pre-existing**: nothing in `ADR-0027` created it, but `pv-gip.5`'s answer
leans on it.

## The gap

`OPS-48`'s third row closes an episode `funded` with no attempt settled: "the exhaustion sweep
finds the machine of a `stalled` episode funded under `OPS-41`'s predicate (a rate rise can do
this with no caller action, and the fence forbids the caller's own) **and its tenant not
suspended** at that read" (`03-operation-lifecycle.md:926`), and clears the fence in the same
transaction.

But the sweep's population is defined by its index: `05-persistence.md:291` gives `machines` an
"index on `(runway_until)` for the exhaustion sweep (`LDG-13`)", and `LDG-16` says the sweep
"MUST route a machine where its stored `runway_until` has passed … and MUST NOT route it
otherwise". A machine a rate rise has just made funded has a **future** `runway_until` and is
exactly the machine that index scan does not return. No requirement says the sweep also visits
the machines of `stalled` episodes. If the scan population is the routing population, the row
can never fire on the machine it describes, and a `stalled` fence has no actor left to clear it —
`OPS-42`'s accepted no-exit ("no verb lifts the fence while the condition stands",
`03:900-901`) reached by a road nobody chose.

The Lean model (`tools/formal/Provisiond/Fence.lean`, `sweep`) checks a stalled episode before
routing on every machine it is given, so the formal layer cannot see the gap: it has no notion of
which machines the sweep enumerates.

## What to decide, then land

Either the sweep's population is stated as two: machines whose stored `runway_until` has passed,
**and** the machines of every open `stalled` episode (`STO-52`'s index gives them) — with the
funded-close row reachable from the second; or the funded close moves to another actor that
already visits stalled episodes. State it in `LDG-13`/`LDG-16` or `OPS-48`, cite the index that
serves it, and give `CNF-99` or `OPS-48`'s items the case: a stalled episode whose machine a rate
rise funds closes `funded` without an operator.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The sweep's population is stated, with the index that serves each part
- [ ] The funded-close row is reachable on a machine whose `runway_until` is in the future, by the
      text, with a conformance case
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, unpiped
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes

comments.text:
Q12 decided 2026-10-04 by the owner ("option 2"): the operator's retry means delete. An attempt
enqueued by `retry` (API-64) on a `stalled` episode makes no OPS-41 funding re-check: the decision
to delete was made when the fence was written, and a price move since does not reverse it (the
suspension exemption is moot: it cancels regardless). Reviving is its own operator verb, "keep":
operator-only, synchronous, idempotent (WIR-24's one-transaction rule), admissible only on a
`stalled` episode; it closes the episode (a new close_reason, e.g. `kept`), clears the fence in the
same transaction, records who and on what evidence (as OPS-31's resolutions do), and writes the
re-derived runway_until as OPS-41's abort does. It does not fund the machine: one still unfunded is
routed again by the next sweep, and the verb's text says so. This gives OPS-42's stated no-exit
("a provider that refuses the delete indefinitely, on a machine that is out of runway, whose
customer wants to pay", 03:977-980) an operator exit. Edits: OPS-48 (a keep row; the retry row says
its attempt skips the re-check), OPS-41 (scope the re-check to attempts not enqueued by retry),
OPS-42's "the route back is the operator's retry" paragraph (03:972-981), API-64/WIR-51 (the verb,
next free ids if new), DOM-31's edge, CNF-271/CNF-272 (retry on a price-funded stalled machine calls
the provider; keep closes, clears the fence, an extension is then admitted; keep on an unfunded
machine is routed at the next sweep), Lean (Fence/Tables/Render: a retried attempt skips the
re-check; the keep transition). An ADR for Q11+Q12 (the owner's principle: deciding to delete is
careful, then irreversible except by an operator decision), rationale only, rejected (A), (B) and
retry-revives.

title: STO-54's grace runs from the restore instant, before a tenant can extend
description:
## Parent

`pv-gip`. Found by the 2026-09-23 panel on the inherited-fence question (`gpt-6-astra`), verified
against `STO-54`. **Pre-existing**: `ADR-0023`'s grace, not `ADR-0027`'s window.

## The gap

`STO-54`'s grace "buys the tenant one re-derivation interval in which to extend again"
(`05-persistence.md:1258`), and the deadline is "the restore instant plus one re-derivation
interval" (`:1202`). But the restore procedure keeps the public listener down through step (1)
and step (2), and public requests wait until step (3) — the watch set re-derived, both rails
replayed, credentials replaced (`:1220`). The interval starts at the restore instant, not at the
instant a tenant can first extend. A restore whose steps (1)–(3) take most of an interval leaves
the tenant a grace they cannot use, and a restore that takes longer than one leaves none.

## What to decide, then land

Key the deadline to the instant extensions become possible — the restore record's step (3) mark
(`STO-56`) — or state in `STO-54` that the grace is measured from the restore instant and may be
consumed by the procedure, so nobody reads "one interval to extend" as a promise of usable time.
Either way, `CNF-99`'s restore case says which instant it measures from.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `STO-54` states which instant the grace is measured from, and why
- [ ] The restore case in the conformance items measures from that instant
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, unpiped
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes
close_reason: dissolved by ADR-0028: the grace runs from step (3) by construction

title: The outage record is the subject's, its start is the currency's, and the meter opens it
description:
## Parent

`pv-gip`. Decided 2026-09-25 and **corrected the same day** in `ADR-0027`'s freshness bullet (the
paragraph beginning "The outage record is the subject's, its start is the currency's, and the
meter opens it"): this ticket's first Run found the first form — one row per currency — contradicted
`STO-37`, `LDG-64`, `LDG-66`, `OPS-41` and `CNF-218`, all of which make the rate-outage row a
subject's. The corrected decision keeps every standing sentence. Pre-existing gap sharpened by
continuous staleness: the set names every closer of `STO-37`'s outage row and never an opener, and
an outage can now begin with no pass running.

## Decided

- **The row is the subject's.** One `STO-37` rate-outage row per machine or attachment per
  outage, as the table's columns and `OPS-41`'s "this machine's open `rate_outage` deficiency
  record" already say. Nothing deployment-wide.
- **Its start is the currency's.** Every row of one currency carries the same `absorbed_from`:
  the instant no rate began for that currency — for staleness, the newest observation's
  `observed_at` plus the staleness bound; for thinness, the `observed_at` of the pass that found the
  window thin (the newest observation is then still fresh, so "newest plus bound" would put the
  start in the future). Arithmetic on `STO-49`'s recorded instants, identical for every writer.
- **The meter opens it.** At a subject's first posting that computes no rate and finds no open row
  for that subject — open meaning `absorbed_until IS NULL` — the meter inserts the row, guarded on
  that absence (not merely keyed), so a reader computing staleness and a pass that finds the window
  thin cannot open two rows for one outage. `outage_deadline` is written in the same insert as
  `absorbed_from` plus `LDG-64`'s bound. The worker's `OPS-41` contend does **not** open a row: its
  affects-no-row branch is how it learns the meter stopped. A create and the solvency check
  compute no rate for no subject and open nothing.
- A late opening changes no bill and no deadline: `LDG-38`'s apportioning and `LDG-64`'s bound
  read the persisted `absorbed_from`.

## What to land

The first Run's Implementer draft is preserved in full in that Run's report
(`.rloop/runs/20260925T*/finished.md`, the diff at the end); its `CNF-99` wording items — "before
any pass accepts an observation", "longer than the cadence plus the read-to-commit lag" with the
`STO-49` quote "a pass that reads early and commits late" — and its `LDG-64` pointer were correct
and uncontested. Reuse them verbatim. Change what the correction changes:

- **`STO-37`** (`05-persistence.md`, beside "opens when there is no rate"): the opening rule as
  Decided — the meter, per subject, guarded on no open row for the subject, the instant per
  currency, the deadline in the same insert. Name the rows that compute the rate rather than "any
  consumer `LDG-40`'s matrix names" (the exhaustion sweep computes none). Say what "open" means:
  `absorbed_until IS NULL`, in `OPS-41`'s words. Dated note quoting `ADR-0027`'s correction once.
- **`LDG-64`**: "persist the outage's start instant" points at `STO-37` for the writer and the
  instant; no second explanation. Quote `LDG-64`'s own close sentence and `LDG-59`'s "The window's
  staleness is tested continuously" where the draft paraphrased them.
- **`CNF-99`**: the silent-feed clause cites `STO-37`; the two wording items above; the
  concurrent-open case becomes **two subjects' meters posting after one outage began** — two
  rows, one `absorbed_from` each, equal, and the sweep's contend on either subject opens nothing;
  the thin-start case pins the staleness bound above the gap since the last accepted observation
  (else the outage began earlier at newest plus bound and a correct build fails the case), and
  adds that an already-open row is preserved — its `absorbed_from` does not move when a later
  reader computes a later start. Fix the two wrap stubs the reviewers found (`an observation**:`
  and `a window that` on lines of their own); drop "never later than the pass".

## Must not touch

`LDG-58`, `LDG-59`'s two clocks (done), `LDG-38`, `STO-54`, `STO-56` (pv-gip.5's), `tools/`,
`docs/adr/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `STO-37` names the opener (the meter, per subject), the guard (no open row for the subject),
      the instant (per currency, both clocks), and the deadline's writer (the same insert)
- [ ] `LDG-64` points at it; `grep -n "keyed on the currency" *.md` is empty
- [ ] `CNF-99`'s three wording items and its two corrected cases landed
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, unpiped
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes
close_reason: Landed by the second Run (Rounds 1-2, four Reviewers each Round): STO-37 names the opener, guard, instant and deadline writer; LDG-64 points at it; CNF-99 carries the three wording items, the two-subjects, thin-start and preserved-row cases. Gate green unpiped. The crossing of the two clocks inside one outage, found by opus in Round 2, is the owner's question and is pv-gip.18, blocking pv-gip.2.

Confirmed real and pre-existing by the two-axis review of 135049a (Spec axis), 2026-09-23. STO-37

title: One start per outage: absorbed_from is the earliest instant of the maximal no-rate interval, replayed from STO-49
description:
## Parent

`pv-gip`. Surfaced by `pv-gip.16`'s second Run; decided 2026-09-25 and recorded in `ADR-0027`'s
freshness bullet (the paragraph beginning "The outage record is the subject's", as amended the
same day). Blocks `pv-gip.2`, which formalizes the instant.

## Decided

**Every row of one outage carries the same `absorbed_from`: the earliest instant of the maximal
interval, ending at the writer's posting, throughout which the window yielded no rate.** It is
computed from `STO-49`'s recorded observations by replaying `LDG-59`'s two clocks over them —
staleness at every instant, thinness at each accepting pass — and is therefore a function of the
history alone: the same for every writer whatever the interleaving of postings and passes, and no
writer reads any sibling row. The two per-clock formulas the first form gave (newest plus bound;
the thin pass's instant) are what that replay yields when only one clock has fired; when the clocks
cross inside one outage — the newest goes stale, a later pass accepts one observation into a
still-thin window — the replay still returns the first instant, which the per-writer formulas did
not. Copying the start from a sibling row was refused: a writer that computed before a thin pass
committed and one that read after it can interleave so neither sees the other.

**`STO-49` retains the rows that establish an open outage's start until the outage closes**, beside
its existing floors, so the replay always has its left edge.

## What to land

- **`STO-37`** (`05-persistence.md`, the opening paragraph landed by `fd3b53a`): the instant's
  definition replaced by the one above, quoting `ADR-0027`'s amended sentence once; the two
  per-clock clauses kept as what the replay yields when one clock fired, not as the rule; "every
  row of one outage" already says "outage". Take the review's three residue points in the same
  edit: the dated note stops re-arguing the paragraph (the ADR pointer plus "named every closer,
  never an opener"); the guard is stated once; `OPS-41`'s affects-no-row argument is pointed at,
  not re-explained. "have no subject to open one for" for the create and the solvency check.
- **`STO-49`**: the retention clause above, dated, beside "never less than one window per
  currency".
- **`LDG-64`**: unchanged unless its pointer's wording no longer matches; check.
- **`CNF-99`**: the crossing case — bound b < cadence c, window 3c; the newest goes stale at t0+b
  and machine A's meter opens at t0+b; sub-quorum passes accept nothing; at t0+3c a pass accepts
  one observation and the window is thin; machine B's first posting lands after it — assert B's
  `absorbed_from` = t0+b = A's, one deadline for both, and that [t0+b, t0+3c) is absorbed for B.
  And the guard case: two concurrent postings of one subject open one row. Fix the wrap stubs the
  review named (`10-conformance-checklist.md` about `:442`, `:456-457`, `:459`;
  `05-persistence.md:880`).
- **`docs/adr/0027-*.md`**: already amended by the deciding commit — not the ticket's.

## Must not touch

`LDG-58`, `LDG-59`'s two clocks, `LDG-38`, `STO-54`, `STO-56`, `OPS-41`, `tools/`, `docs/adr/`.
`pv-gip.19` (`absorbed_seconds`'s writer) is separate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `STO-37` defines the start as the history-replayed earliest instant, one sentence, and
      names the per-clock formulas as its special cases
- [ ] `STO-49` carries the outage-start retention clause
- [ ] `CNF-99` carries the crossing case and the concurrent-guard case; the crossing case's

title: absorbed_seconds has no named writer; absorbed_until 'required wherever non-zero' against 'open means null'
description:
## Parent

`pv-gip`. Pre-existing; noted by opus in `pv-gip.16`'s second Run, Round 1, as outside that
ticket's scope.

## The gap

`STO-37`'s column note says `absorbed_until` is "required wherever `absorbed_seconds` is non-zero",
and the same requirement now says a rate-outage row is open while "`absorbed_until IS NULL`"
(`OPS-41`'s guard, rendered 2026-09-25). Whether those collide depends on when `absorbed_seconds`
is written, and no sentence in the set names its writer: `grep -rn absorbed_seconds --include='*.md'`
returns seven hits, none a writer. `LDG-38` subtracts it and `LDG-66` requires it carried; `LDG-64`
names the writer of `absorbed_until` (the observation that produces a rate again, or the subject's
meter stop) and not of the seconds.

## What to decide

Who writes `absorbed_seconds`, and when — most simply, the same write that closes the window
(`absorbed_until`'s writer), as `absorbed_until - absorbed_from`, so a row is open with the seconds
at zero and the column note's "required wherever non-zero" holds by construction. State it in
`STO-37` beside the column, and point `LDG-64`'s close bullet at it if the writer is that write.

title: The formal layer: the median theorem as LDG-16's home; the reference and deadline models deleted; the grace as the record's one instant
description:
## Parent

`pv-gip`. Blocked by `pv-gip.5` and `pv-gip.16`: the rules land first; this models what they say.
Absorbs what remains of `pv-vwe.22` (its third site only; the first two dissolved with `ADR-0028`).

## What to build

**A rate module**, the formal home of `LDG-16`'s promise. The lower median over a list of accepted
observations, and the theorem `ADR-0027` names: *replacing any one observation in the window cannot
move the median past a value another observation in the window carries.* Tagged `@[req "LDG-58"]`
for the median and `@[req "LDG-16"]` for the promise, so `check_formal` renders them where the
requirement is read. Plain lists, no Mathlib (the toolchain has none). State the no-rate cases —
fewer than three at the pass, none inside the staleness bound at any instant — as the function's
`none`, on the two clocks `LDG-59` states. The theorem is about one observation; do not state or
tag anything stronger than `ADR-0027`'s "What this does not promise" allows.

**The reference model deleted.** In `Provisiond.Fence`: `rederiveFacts` loses its reference half
and its acceptance-order confirmation; `World.routed` loses the reference clause and, with it, the
`Params` argument it regained for `noAgeDischarge`; the controls `armWinsFutureClear`,
`confirmationByOrder`, `backwardCannotConfirm` and `noAgeDischarge` go with the rules they put
back, and so do their witnesses and their `ci.yml` rows — remove rows, never edit a count: the list
holds its own number since `f3ec74c`. `legacyArmedAt` goes; it was ghost history for those
controls. `armed_reference_not_routed` goes with `LDG-65`'s clause. `Admission.lean`'s `LDG-40`
pointer is re-aimed at the no-observation branch that remains and the routing predicate.
`machines.rateConfirmationRef` leaves the machine row.

**The deadline model deleted** (`ADR-0028`). `destroyNotBefore` leaves the machine row;
`World.routed` is the stored date alone; `providerDelete`'s gate and `provider_waits_for_deadline`
go; `observationKeepsDeadline` and its witness go; `restoreGrace` and `rederiveFacts`'s deadline
field go. `Restore.lean`'s grace is the record's one instant, `grace_ends_at`, written at step (3)
as that instant plus one interval — one home, which dissolves `pv-vwe.22`'s second site. The
claim guard: a claim of an exposure-reducing cancellation while the open restore record's instant
is in the future returns the operation to `queued` with `available_at` at that instant, the same
write as `OPS-8`'s defer — modelled where `OPS-8`'s defer already is, in `Claim`, reading the
restore record; `Fence` composes on it. Every docstring that quotes `LDG-16`, `LDG-41`, `LDG-62`,
`LDG-64`, `LDG-65`, `OPS-41`, `PRV-13e`, `STO-49`, `STO-54` or `STO-56` is re-quoted against the
text `pv-gip.5` and `pv-gip.16` landed; the citations gate reads these docstrings only where a
speech verb attributes them, so read them all.

**`pv-vwe.22`'s surviving site.** `agedWorld` is checked to still trap what it trapped, and its
docstring says what that is.

## Red builds

- The withdrawn rule that the rate is the **newest** observation rather than the window's lower
  median: one `Params` field, one `ci.yml` row, one witness whose window is honest `100`s with a
  poisoned `103` as its newest pass, on a machine pinned at the edge where at `103` `usable_sats`
  clamps to `0` and `runway_until` lands in the past while at `100` it stays future; the trace runs
  the whole lifecycle to `providerDelete` — destroyed with the field off, survives with it on.
- The withdrawn per-machine deadline, as the trap `ADR-0028` names — its **placement**, not its
  arithmetic: one `Params` field named for the current rule, `graceAtClaim`, `true` in `current`.
  With it on, a claim of an exposure-reducing cancellation during an open restore's grace defers
  and writes no fence; with it off, the withdrawn form runs — the claim proceeds, fences, and the
  guard sits on the provider call. The witness: a restore, a delete re-run by step (2), a tenant
  who extends after step (3). Under `current` the extension lands (`destroy_committed` is null)
  and the re-claim closes `funded`; under the withdrawn form the fence refuses the extension for
  the whole grace and the machine is destroyed after it. Destroyed with the field off, survives
  with it on. Pin the field on in every other witness that runs a restore, so the flip reds
  exactly this one.

## Must not touch

`Meter`, `Ledger`, `Rescue`, `Wire`, `Admission`'s matrices beyond the one pointer. Every surviving
`ci.yml` row keeps exactly one red per flip, rehearsed locally before the push.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The rate module with the median theorem, tagged as `LDG-16`'s and `LDG-58`'s home
- [ ] `grep -rn "rateConfirmationRef\|legacyArmedAt\|noAgeDischarge\|confirmationByOrder\|armWinsFutureClear\|backwardCannotConfirm\|destroyNotBefore\|observationKeepsDeadline\|provider_waits_for_deadline" tools/` is empty
- [ ] The two new negative controls red exactly one witness each; every surviving row still reds
      exactly one
- [ ] The restore grace has one home in the model; `pv-vwe.22` closed with its comment saying so
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, unpiped, and the docstrings re-quoted
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes

title: CNF-99: a b > 3c variant asserting the last rate pass's snapshot survives sub-quorum passes
description:
## Parent

`pv-gip`. Filed from the Round 2 review of `pv-gip.18` (sol), 2026-09-25.

## The gap

`STO-49`'s outage-start retention floor (landed by `pv-gip.18`) is prospective: it keeps the rows
inside the window as of the last accepting pass that yielded a rate, and every row accepted since,
so that an outage that begins later — by thinness at an accepting pass after sub-quorum passes, or
by staleness with a bound longer than the cadence — still replays that pass as a rate. `CNF-99`'s
crossing case (`b < c`) does not exercise that: there the staleness clock fires before any
pre-outage row leaves the one-window floor.

## What to land

A `CNF-99` variant: window `3c`, staleness bound `b > 3c`; passes at `t0−2c`, `t0−c`, `t0` yield
a rate; passes at `t0+c`, `t0+2c` fall below `LDG-59`'s quorum; every subject closes an increment
past `t0−c`; at `t0+3c` an accepting pass finds the window thin. Assert the rows `t0−2c`, `t0−c`
and `t0` are still present at `t0+3c`, and that a subject posting after `t0+3c` opens a row with
`absorbed_from = t0+3c`, not earlier.

title: STO-49: the one-window floor is subsumed by the outage-start floor; collapse or say so
description:
## Parent

`pv-gip`. Filed from the Round 3 review of `pv-gip.18` (opus), 2026-09-25.

## The observation

`STO-49` now carries three retention floors. Under `LDG-58`'s anchor — the window is "the last
window-length before the pass that computed the rate", and "Each pass that accepts an observation
computes the rate over the window as of that pass" — the second floor ("never less than one window
per currency") holds the rows in `(Q−W, Q]` for the last accepting pass `Q`. The third floor
(the outage-start floor, `pv-gip.18`) holds `(P−W, P]` plus every row accepted since `P`, for the
last accepting pass `P ≤ Q` that yielded that currency's rate. The third is a superset of the
second in every case the reviewer could construct, so the second has no work left to do.

Related: `ADR-0027`'s sentence "`STO-49` retains the rows that establish an open outage's start
until the outage closes" is true but no longer the whole rule, since the floor holds them before
any outage exists. `docs/adr/` is the owner's.

## What to decide

Whether to collapse the second floor into the third — one sentence, one dated note recording
that the one-window floor is subsumed — or to keep both and say which one holds when they differ
(they should not). Prose only; `STO-49` only; `pv-gip.18`'s floor is the one to keep.

title: ADR-0029: during a price outage a funding cancellation waits for the rate or the outage bound
description:
Raised by pv-gip.2's Round-1 review (opus, 2026-09-25), from the model rather than the text.

## What was found

`OPS-41` distinguishes its two no-rate outcomes by the conditional write on `STO-37`'s record:
"Where that write affects a row the outage is still open for this machine and the cancel
proceeds. Where it affects no row, something closed the window first: where a rate now exists —
restoration (`LDG-64`) — the worker re-derives at it and applies the ordinary predicate above, and
where none does the machine's own meter stopped (`LDG-74`), there is nothing left to cancel".

`STO-37` says the meter "opens it at a subject's first posting that computes no rate and finds no
open row for that subject". So between the instant the window stops yielding a rate and that
subject's first posting, the row does not exist yet. A worker claiming in that interval finds no
rate and a write that affects no row, and `OPS-41`'s third branch reads that as a stopped meter —
on a machine whose meter is running and whose outage has just begun. The branch settles the
cancellation as the no-mutation case.

The two states are indistinguishable to the worker: 'the row was never opened' and 'the row was
closed because the subject died' are both zero rows.

## Why it is filed rather than fixed

`pv-gip.2` models the rate as `LDG-58`'s window (`Provisiond.Rate`), so a thin or stale window is
now a first-class way to reach rate = none with no outage row open; the model made the gap visible.
The repair is a requirement's, not the model's: either `OPS-41` gains a term that separates the two
zero-row cases, or `LDG-74`'s meter-stop is given a fact the worker can read, or the branch is
argued safe because the window is narrow. `LDG-13` and `LDG-40` ("the exhaustion sweep MUST
continue: it reduces exposure") are what the current reading costs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `OPS-41`'s zero-row branch either distinguishes the two states or says in its own text why the
      transient is safe, with the argument and not an assertion
- [ ] Whatever lands is reflected in `Provisiond.Fence`'s `readRate`, which carries the branch
close_reason: ADR-0029 landed in the requirements and the conformance checklist, two rloop Rounds, four-model Panel each; gate green unpiped. Formal layer is pv-gip.25. Follow-ups pv-gip.26 to pv-gip.30.

comments.author: master
comments.text: Decided 2026-10-01 by the owner after two panels (opus/astra/sol 2026-09-27; fable/astra/sol 2026-10-01), recorded as ADR-0029: a funding cancellation waits while its currency has no rate, until the rate returns or the outage bound. Shape: the sweep routes a funding cancellation only where the date has passed AND the currency has a rate; the worker decides inside the fence transaction (gone/closed -> settle; suspended -> proceed; rate -> re-derive; no rate before the deadline -> OPS-8 short defer, no fence; at/after the deadline -> contend on the record and proceed). The deadline is computed from STO-49's history (start + bound). The bound reaches every subject priced in the currency. An extension halts with no rate. Accepted costs: broke-before-outage machines carried to the bound; flapping feed capped per outage; notice-period contracts may cost one period; restore grace composes as the later instant. The edit list is ADR-0029's Consequences. Open: whether STO-37's persisted outage_deadline stays as a copy or is deleted.

title: Residue of pv-gip.2: the grace witness's fixed advance, its unasserted deferral, two docstring points
description:
Four polish points raised by the Round-3 Panel (fable, opus) on `pv-gip.2`'s landed work. None is a
defect: the gate is green, every `ci.yml` row reds exactly one witness, and every assertion holds.

## The points

1. **`graceTrace`'s advance is a literal, not a function of the instant it must cross.**
   `Provisiond.Witnesses.graceTrace` opens `[.claim, .fenceTxn, .fenceWrite, .advance 30, …]`, where
   `30` is `stepThreeAt - restoredWorld.now` — 80 minus 50. If either number moves, the trace stops
   crossing step (3) and the witness quietly stops demonstrating what its docstring says: the
   extension inside the grace rather than before step (3). `.advance (stepThreeAt - 50)`, or an
   assertion that the clock equals `stepThreeAt` at that point, would pin it.

2. **The first claim's deferral is asserted by its absence of effect.** `grace_at_claim_witness`
   asserts `phase = .idle` and `m.fence = none` after `[.claim]`, which would also hold had the claim
   been refused outright rather than claimed and deferred. `Provisiond.Fence.grace_defers_without_fence`
   proves the row is `queued` again in general, so the witness could assert the row's status or its
   advanced revision and close the gap.

3. **`graceTrace`'s docstring narrates the good run only.** Under `current` four of its fourteen
   events are inert — the `fenceTxn`/`fenceWrite` pair after the deferred claim, and the
   `providerDelete`/`settle` pair before the re-claim — and they are in the trace so the withdrawn
   placement has something to fence and dispatch. A reader following the current rule meets four
   events that do nothing and has to reach the witness's own docstring to learn why.

4. **`Provisiond.Claim`'s module docstring wraps badly.** In the *what the model omits* list,
   "what reads `available_at`," breaks across lines leaving a two-word line mid-list.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The grace trace crosses step (3) by construction, not by two literals agreeing
- [ ] The first claim's deferral is asserted as a deferral
- [ ] Both docstring points addressed
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, unpiped, and every `ci.yml` row still
      reds exactly one witness

title: ADR-0029 in the formal layer: the outage wait, the five-step precedence, extend halts with no rate
description:
Land ADR-0029 in the formal layer, after pv-gip.23 lands it in the requirements. The model is how the
last two decisions were checked: pv-gip.23 itself was exposed by pv-gip.2's model, so this Run is
expected to find gaps in the landed text and report them rather than paper over them.

## What to build

- `Provisiond.Fence.sweep`: route a funding cancellation only where the stored date has passed AND
  the machine's currency has a rate.
- `readRate` / `recheck`: ADR-0029's five-step precedence, decided at the fence transaction (not the
  claim snapshot): gone or closed episode settles; a suspended tenant proceeds; a rate re-derives;
  no rate before the deadline defers by OPS-8's short delay with no fence; no rate at or after the
  deadline contends on the record and proceeds, zero rows with no rate included. The `meterStopped`
  outcome is deleted.
- The deadline as a function of history (the outage's start plus the bound), not a stored field.
- `extend`: halts with no rate, matching `Provisiond.Admission`'s `.extendRunway => .halts`; the two
  models currently disagree, and that disagreement is part of what this closes.
- `Provisiond.Admission`: the `sweepContinuesWithoutRate` guard and the theorem that no
  exposure-reducing action halts for want of a rate, restated for funding cancellations.

## Red builds

- The fresh-outage trace: no rate, no record, a live machine, an open episode. Today it settles as
  no-mutation and the sweep re-queues it; under ADR-0029 it defers and later proceeds at the bound.
- A suspension joining a deferred funding attempt proceeds within one short delay.
- A rate returning one second after the deadline re-derives (CNF-218's restoration case).
- Each new Params field gets a ci.yml row whose flip reds exactly one witness.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every ADR-0029 rule modelled, or named in the module's omissions with the reason
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, unpiped; every ci.yml row rehearsed
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes
close_reason: done

title: extend-runway has three refusals and no order between them (no rate, cancellation_committed, solvency)
description:

title: OPS-36's attach transaction has no rule for a currency with no rate
description:
Raised by pv-gip.23's Round-1 review (sol, and the Implementer, 2026-10-02). Predates ADR-0029; ADR-0029 does not decide it.

## What was found

`OPS-36`'s attach transaction tests available balance against the wind-down floor and either opens a commitment of that size or books the wind-down as an operator deficiency, then enqueues the cleanup. The floor is priced in satoshis at the current rate (`LDG-33`), and `LDG-59` says "Falling back to the last known rate MUST NOT happen". With no rate for the machine's currency the transaction has no specified way to choose its branch or size either record. `LDG-40`'s matrix has no row for it.

pv-gip.23 kept the conformance case off this ground: `CNF-218`'s late-attach cleanup is "enqueued by its attach transaction while a rate existed". `LDG-16` says only that such a cleanup waits at `OPS-41`'s order while there is no rate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `OPS-36` (or `LDG-40`'s matrix, with `OPS-36` pointing at it) says what a late attach does while its currency has no rate
- [ ] A conformance item exercises a correlator match arriving during an outage

title: A replay parameter changed mid-outage: absorbed_from across rows, STO-49 retention, the quorum, and their conformance
description:
Raised by pv-gip.23's reviews (opus, sol, fable, 2026-10-02). ADR-0029 decides that the deadline uses the setting in force; it does not decide these.

## What was found

`OVR-19` (landed by pv-gip.23): the maximum tolerated rate outage "and the staleness bound, window and quorum an outage's start is replayed with (`STO-37`), are each read at the value in force when `LDG-64`'s deadline is computed, for an outage already open too". ADR-0029 says "The record keeps its billing fields". Three things follow that no requirement decides:

1. **`absorbed_from` across rows.** `STO-37` now says the rows of one outage agree "While the parameters the start is replayed with are unchanged". A row opened before a staleness-bound change and one opened after it can carry different `absorbed_from` for one outage, and `LDG-38` then apportions the two machines' relief over different windows. title: After an outage a tenant whose extension was halted has one short delay to extend
description:
Raised by pv-gip.23's Round-1 review (fable, 2026-10-02). Follows from two ADR-0029 decisions together; the owner has not been shown the combination.

## What was found

ADR-0029: "An extension halts with no rate", justified by "no funding cancellation proceeds before the bound, so no customer needs to extend mid-outage to keep a machine". And: a deferred attempt re-decides at every claim, by `OPS-8`'s short delay. Together: a tenant whose funding cancellation was deferred through the outage cannot extend during it, and once the rate returns the deferred attempt is re-claimed within one short delay and cancels on the ordinary predicate. The tenant's whole window to extend is that short delay. Three cases:

- `OPS-36`'s late-attach cleanup — `OPS-36` says "**Survival requires a caller action**: the tenant may `extend-runway`";
- a restore during an outage — the grace exists so a tenant whose extension the restore lost can extend again, and it can expire inside the outage with every extension refused;
- a machine whose attempt was queued before the outage began.

pv-gip.23 removed the sentence "No customer needs an extension mid-outage to keep a machine" from `LDG-62` (it is ADR-0029's argument and has these counterexamples) and added nothing about the window.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The owner decides whether the post-restoration window is accepted as it is (and ADR-0029's accepted costs say so) or a deferred attempt waits some stated time after the rate returns
- [ ] `OPS-36`'s survival sentence and `STO-54`'s grace say what the outage does to them, by pointer

title: ADR-0027's two amendments in the requirements: the rate is computed at a pass, and one pass below quorum halts nothing
description:
## Parent

`pv-gip` — the window median (`ADR-0027`). Opened by `pv-gip.1`'s Run as an owner's clarification;
both questions are now decided (2026-09-23) and recorded as dated amendments in `ADR-0027`'s
Decision. This ticket lands them in the requirements. `pv-gip.9`'s record points ride along, since
they touch the same files.

## Decided

**The rate is computed at a pass and holds until the next.** Each pass that accepts an observation
recomputes the lower median over the observations whose `observed_at` lies inside the window
*as of that pass*; between passes the rate does not move, so an observation ageing out of the
window changes nothing until a pass recomputes. Every change of rate therefore lands on an
instant with a durable `STO-49` row, and `LDG-38`'s split rule and its "durable before the rate is
used" requirement stand exactly as written. The rate in force at any instant is the one the
latest pass at or before it computed — recomputable from `STO-49`'s rows, which the one-window
retention floor keeps; no new column.

**One pass below quorum halts nothing.** It accepts no observation and recomputes nothing, so the
rate in force holds. `LDG-59`'s quorum decides whether a pass accepts an observation; **no rate**
— `LDG-40`'s input — arises only from the window: nothing inside the staleness bound, or fewer
than three observations. A blip rides through; an outage that outlasts the bound halts as today.

## What to land

- **`LDG-58`** (`12-billing-and-ledger.md` ~`:1081-1082`): "whose `observed_at` lies inside the
  last window-length **before now**" becomes "before the pass that computed the rate", plus one
  sentence: the rate is computed at each accepting pass over the window as of that pass and holds
  until the next; an observation ageing out changes nothing on its own. Dated note.
- **`LDG-59`** (~`:1085-1097`): the quorum sentence stops saying "below which there is **no
  rate**" and says a pass below quorum accepts no observation and the rate in force holds; the
  "A window can **also** produce no rate … these are new inputs" paragraph becomes the *only*
  source of no rate. Retain the withdrawn per-pass halt wording in the dated note — it stood from
  2026-09-05 to 2026-09-23 and is the trap `ADR-0027` names (a halt handed to whoever disrupts one
  pass).
- **`LDG-40`** (halt matrix): its trigger sentence, if it names the quorum, names the window's
  no-rate instead; the matrix's rows do not change.
- **`LDG-64`**: already keyed to "the window producing a rate again" by `pv-gip.1`; confirm the
  wording matches — a pass restoring quorum is not by itself a rate.
- **`CNF-99`**: two cases — a sub-quorum pass with a fresh window leaves purchases and re-pricing
  running at the rate in force; an observation ageing out mid-increment changes no bill until the
  next pass. The existing no-fresh and thin cases stand.
- **`CONTEXT.md`** already says both (**Window**, **Quorum**); if the Run finds the glossary and
  the rule disagree, the rule is wrong.
- **`pv-gip.9`'s three points**, verbatim from that ticket: `STO-54`'s 2026-09-23 note moved
  after the 2026-09-21 record; `LDG-41`'s note stops re-arguing `LDG-16`'s withdrawal; `LDG-41`'s
  heading either drops "(`ADR-0011`)" or dates it as a 2026-09-23 clarification.

## Must not touch

`LDG-38` — untouched by design; that is the point of the first decision. `tools/`, `docs/adr/`.
`OPS-41`/`OPS-48` are `pv-gip.5`'s.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `grep -n "before now" 12-billing-and-ledger.md` is empty
- [ ] `LDG-59` contains no sentence making a pass's quorum loss "no rate"; the withdrawn wording is
      in its dated note
- [ ] `CNF-99` carries the two new cases
- [ ] `pv-gip.9` closed by this diff, its three points landed
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, unpiped
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes

title: LDG-40's solvency row is not scoped by currency: a one-currency outage against LDG-59's 'halts nothing priced in EUR'
description:
Raised by the residue Round on pv-gip.23 (2026-10-02): the Implementer and all four Reviewers
(fable, opus, astra, sol) read it the same way. Owner's decision; pre-existing, not made by
ADR-0029.

## What was found

Three sentences, as the set stands:

- `LDG-40`: "**the solvency check** (MUST fail closed)" when no rate is available — with no
  currency clause, where the sweep's row beside it is scoped ("MUST route no machine priced in that
  currency").
- `LDG-20`: "**On failure the system MUST halt top-ups first**, then refuse every bill-increasing
  operation, while continuing to permit cancellation and deletion."
- `LDG-59`: "there is one rate, one quorum, one outage and one bound for each currency the
  deployment bills in, a subject's rate is its offer's currency, and a USD quorum loss halts
  nothing priced in EUR".

With USD in outage and EUR priced, the first two read together refuse an EUR create or
`extend-runway` (`halted`, `gate: "solvency"`), which `LDG-59`'s sentence denies. Two readings,
two behaviours: the solvency check fails closed deployment-wide whenever any billed currency has
no rate, or its failure is scoped so that an outage in one currency halts nothing priced in
another (and then what the check does with payables in the currency it cannot convert is
unstated).

## What it costs today

`CNF-138`'s two-currency case (added in the residue Round) asserts only that the healthy
currency's `extend-runway` "is not refused with `gate: "rate_unavailable"`", and says it asserts
nothing about the solvency check. A build that refuses that extension under `gate: "solvency"`
passes the clause; only the sweep and worker clauses catch a deployment-wide halt. `pv-gip.26`
holds the order of `extend-runway`'s refusals, not their currency scope.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One requirement states what the solvency check does while one billed currency has no rate
      and another has one, and `LDG-40`'s row and `LDG-59`'s sentence agree with it
- [ ] `CNF-138`'s two-currency case asserts the decided outcome for a create and an
      `extend-runway` in the healthy currency (admitted, or refused with the stated gate)

title: LDG-16's routing predicate has no state clause, so a machine recorded gone is re-routed every sweep pass
description:
Raised by the Spec axis of the review of `bea081c` (2026-10-02), extending opus's note on
`pv-gip.11` (comment there). Pre-existing; not introduced by ADR-0029, which made it easier to reach.

## What was found

`LDG-16`'s predicate (`12-billing-and-ledger.md` ~1652) routes a machine where its stored
`runway_until` has passed and its currency has a rate. It has no state clause. A machine recorded
gone (`LDG-74`'s gone-write) keeps a past `runway_until`, since none of the date's writers runs on
it (`05-persistence.md` ~266), and `OPS-41` step 1 now settles its attempt while writing no date.
So once a rate exists the sweep routes it, `OPS-39` opens a fresh episode (the closed one does not
block a new one), and step 1 settles it again, every pass. The same holds for every machine an
ordinary exhaustion delete tombstoned (`STO-8`). The checklist already assumes a tombstoned machine
is not routed (`10-conformance-checklist.md` ~1257–1259), and `Provisiond.Fence.sweep` already
carries `!w.m.gone`, but no requirement says so. `LDG-64`'s bound population ("every machine priced
in the outage's currency") has the same question.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `LDG-16`'s predicate (or its owner) excludes a machine recorded gone, quoting `LDG-74`'s
      "a machine established gone has nothing left to cancel"
- [ ] `LDG-64`'s bound population says the same
- [ ] A `CNF` case: a machine recorded gone with a past date opens no episode on the next pass

title: "Has passed" at the instant itself: OPS-41's deadline and LDG-16's stored date do not say whether equality counts
description:

- [ ] If the answer is not "reached is passed", `deadlinePassed`/`routed` and the witnesses at the

title: A rate return between claim and fence transaction bypasses paused restore grace
description:
Found in the Manager's Round-1 review of pv-gip.29, landing ad6e2d9.

OPS-41 (03-operation-lifecycle.md:752) says: "After that wall-clock end, while a rate exists and a funding cancellation has unspent grace, the claim MUST return the attempt to `queued`". Its composition says "the grace is read first, at the claim"; the ordered worker decision is "inside the fence transaction and on what that transaction reads, never on its claim snapshot". The owner's decision promises an interval of rate-present time, but the no-rate claim can enter a transaction that sees a returned rate and cancels without another grace read.

Reproduction in the landed Lean model: run Fence.current on pausedGraceWorld with [.rateLost 80, .advance 120, .claim, .pass [1, 1, 1] 80, .fenceTxn, .providerDelete true (some true)]. At time 200 the result is destroyed = true, rateHistory = [(80,200)], rateTime since step (3) = 0, and graceDefers on the resulting world = true. The original end is 140, the interval 60, and the outage bound is later. Evidence: /var/tmp/provisiond-manager-r1-race.lean and /var/tmp/provisiond-manager-r1-race.log; `nix develop --command lake env lean /var/tmp/provisiond-manager-r1-race.lean` in tools/formal exits 0.

Owner clarification required: is claim-only grace intentionally allowed to lose this race, or must an attempt admitted with no rate re-enter/validate the grace before a funding cancellation uses a returned rate? These produce different destruction behavior. Recommend preserving the accumulated grace promise, explicitly qualifying the claim-only rule for this interleaving; implementation method remains open.

Acceptance: record the owner's choice in OPS-41/ADR-0029, align the composed model, and add a conformance case and executable witness for return between claim and fence transaction. Do not silently add a second normative rule or merely change the witness order.
