title: A queued paused-grace deferral can delay a later outage bound or suspension
description:
Found by Sol and confirmed by the Manager during Round 1 of pv-gip.29, landing ad6e2d9.

OPS-41 (03-operation-lifecycle.md:752-755) mandates `available_at` equal to "now + (one re-derivation interval − accumulated rate-present time)". OPS-6 says "The claim MUST select the oldest `queued` operation whose availability time has passed." OPS-39 says "a sweep MUST enqueue nothing against a machine whose episode under that key is open". LDG-64 says "cancel machines at that bound" if no rate has returned. OPS-41 says the current suspension and bound "retain the original wall-clock grace only".

Trace: the original wall-clock end has passed; a return and claim at 100 compute paused end 160 and queue the attempt until then. A new outage starts at 101, with bound 110. The existing attempt cannot claim at 110 and the bound cannot enqueue a second attempt for that episode. A suspension joining after the claim similarly cannot act before 160. Nothing currently advances availability on these events. The Lean Claim model explicitly omits the reader of available_at, so its theorem about a claim at the bound does not establish that the queue permits that claim.

Owner clarification required: retain the specified deferral instant and accept that later bound/suspension actions wait for it, or require those later actions to supersede a queued paused-grace deferral? The original work order mandates the deferral instant and the exception, while the brief excludes redesigning wake-ups; selecting an exception changes the specifications. Recommend preserving the bound/current-suspension exception, with an explicit rule making already-deferred attempts eligible when it applies. Do not pick a wake-up implementation before the behavior is decided.

Acceptance: decide this composition in the normative owners and ADR, and add a queue-eligibility-aware conformance trace for both a new outage/bound and current suspension after available_at was set. A test that manually claims a not-yet-available attempt does not cover the defect.

title: Bound-based restore closure can discard grace for a still-queued funding cancellation
description:
Found by Sol and confirmed by the Manager during Round 1 of pv-gip.29, landing ad6e2d9.

STO-56 (05-persistence.md:1141-1148) permits closure when, for each currency, "either its accumulated rate-present time since step (3) has reached one re-derivation interval (`OPS-41`) or its outage has reached `LDG-64`'s bound" and asserts "no funding cancellation remains to protect past that bound". OPS-41 says "With no open restore record there is no restore-grace deferral." Its ordered worker decision applies the ordinary predicate when a rate exists. The owner's work order explicitly prescribed the bound-based close exception using that premise.

Trace: after the original wall-clock end, an active unfenced machine's queued attempt short-defers with no rate. The bound arrives before the next claim. All other incident obligations are done, so the operator closes the record. The rate returns before that queued attempt next claims. It now takes the funding re-check without any restore grace and can destroy the machine after less than one interval of rate-present time. Reaching a bound has not itself disposed of this attempt. The same issue can involve a provider refusal or an attempt awaiting availability; the simple queued trace suffices.

Owner clarification required: does merely reaching the bound irrevocably end restore protection for all affected machines, including an attempt that later sees a returned rate, or may incident closure use this exception only once the remaining protected work has a specified disposition? These are different promises. Recommend preserving protection for pending funding cancellations until a disposition or grace completion justifies closure, while retaining a finite escape for a currency that never regains a rate. The owner must settle that tradeoff; do not invent a new stored disposition or close criterion as an implementation detail.

Acceptance: make STO-56's premise and permitted closure match the chosen behavior; reconcile OPS-41 and ADR-0029; add the return-after-close-before-next-claim conformance trace. Do not claim current Lean proofs establish closure: the model explicitly omits it.

title: LDG-16 still identifies restore grace with its unpaused wall-clock end
description:
Found independently by Fable and Opus and verified by the Manager in Round 1 of pv-gip.29, landing ad6e2d9.

LDG-16 (12-billing-and-ledger.md:1726-1727), current normative prose, says: "A restore's grace is no clause of this predicate: it is `STO-56`'s `grace_ends_at`, `OPS-41` holds the rule that defers the claim until it". STO-56 now says "`grace_ends_at` is the unpaused end of the restore grace". OPS-41 now requires a funding cancellation with a returned rate and unspent grace to defer beyond that instant. LDG-16 therefore describes the obsolete wall-clock-only rule as current behavior.

title: A rate_outage deficiency feeds provider payables forever: nothing resolves it
description:
Raised by two readers (fable, opus) of the 2026-10-03 panel on pv-gip.31; holds whichever way that question is decided.

LDG-66 (12-billing-and-ledger.md ~1285-1286): unresolved deficiencies 'MUST feed provider payables in the solvency check (LDG-17)'. So every outage's absorbed provider cost stays a payable in LDG-17's inequality after the outage ends and after the provider has been paid: the phantom liability 05 ~876-878 records for wind-down, again.

Trace: a 6-hour USD outage absorbs 40 USD of provider cost; the operator pays the provider's invoice; the 40 USD row still counts as owed in every later solvency check, forever, and accumulates across outages until the check fails on liabilities already paid.

Acceptance: one requirement says when a rate_outage deficiency stops feeding payables (e.g. when the provider cost it records is paid, or at an operator resolution), STO-37's 'stays null' agrees with it, and a CNF case asserts a settled outage no longer counts.

title: ADR-0027's prose promise overstates its theorem: a poison between two honest prices becomes the median
description:
## Parent

`pv-gip` — the window median (`ADR-0027`). Raised by the Panel reviewing `pv-gip.1` (2026-09-23,
`gpt-6-astra` and `gpt-5.6-sol` independently, verified by arithmetic).

## What is false

`ADR-0027`'s Decision section says a transient bad observation "cannot move the rate to a price
no honest pass in the window accepted". Counterexample: honest `[100, 103, 104]`, replace 103
with 101.5; the lower median is 101.5, a price no honest pass accepted. The theorem the ADR names
— *replacing any one observation in the window cannot move the median past a value another
observation in the window carries* — is a **range** bound and is true; the prose claim that the
rate is always an honest price is stronger than the theorem and false.

`pv-gip.1` landed the true form and flagged it: `LDG-16` says a transient bad observation "moves
the rate (`LDG-58`) no further than to a neighbouring price some honest pass in the window
accepted"; `PRV-13e` says "No single rate observation moves the rate outside what the window's
other observations carry". The ADRs were out of that ticket's scope.

The ADR is also split on "half": its Decision says "at least half the window", its *What this
does not promise* says "more than half". The requirements say half / at least half, which is
correct for a lower median (two of four suffice).

## What to land

- Amend `ADR-0027`'s prose to the range bound the theorem supports, with a dated note recording
  the interior-poison counterexample.
- Make its "half" consistent with the requirements.
- Consider an interior-poison case in `CNF-99` (`[100, 103, 104] → [100, 101.5, 104]`, assert
  the rate is 101.5 and lies inside the honest range): the current far-below case never shows the
  poison itself becoming the median.
- `pv-gip.2` must state its theorem as the range bound, not the ADR's prose.
close_reason: ADR-0027 restated to the range bound the requirements carry

comments.author: master
comments.text:
Fixed in the ADR, 2026-09-23. The three sentences that said "a price no honest pass accepted"
now say the range bound the requirements landed: no further than the honest values on either side,
never outside the range the honest passes carry -- and the ADR carries the counterexample itself
(honest 100, 103, 104; 103 replaced by 101.5 reads 101.5) as the reason the bound is a range and
not a membership. "More than half" is now "half" everywhere, matching the lower median on an even
window. PRV-13e's second half in the ADR is restated as "a rate outside what the honest passes
carry needs at least half the window to carry it", which is the true form; pv-gip.1 landed the
requirement's wording as "No single rate observation moves the rate outside what the window's
other observations carry", and LDG-16's "no further than to a neighbouring price some honest pass
in the window accepted" -- the two-axis review of e7ab053 is checking whether that LDG-16 phrase is
itself true of 101.5 (it is a neighbouring price, but no honest pass accepted it), and if not that
lands with pv-gip.1's record fixes.

the next CNF-99 edit. Closing; pv-gip.2 now waits on pv-gip.3 instead, since Q2 there (does one

title: Historical outage time has no subject row when the first posting follows rate return
description:
## Historical no-rate time without a subject outage row

Found while reviewing pv-vwe.34 exit closure, but pre-existing for ordinary ticks. This is
specification-path analysis, not a running-system test. Verified with whitespace-normalized
`git show` at both `2dc303b` and `736b5c3`, before the follow-up specification edits.

`STO-37` at both revisions defines the replayed start as "the earliest instant of the maximal
interval, ending at the writer's posting, throughout which the window yielded no rate" and opens
a row at the subject's "first posting that computes no rate". `736b5c3` additionally names an
exit posting. `LDG-38` at both revisions says "The window is read from the deficiency record's
`absorbed_from` and `absorbed_until`".

## Reproduction traces

- Exit: mark 12:00; no posting during currency outage 12:20–12:50; scheduled effective
  cancellation 12:40; gone observation and closing writer at 13:00. The increment clips at
  12:40 and contains historical no-rate time, but a rate exists at the writer's posting instant
  and no subject outage row was opened.
- Ordinary tick: mark 12:00; no posting during the same outage 12:20–12:50; tick at 13:00.
  Its elapsed span contains the same historical no-rate time with no row. Also run a scheduled
  subject's tick clipped at the same 12:40 stop boundary to isolate tick versus exit behavior.

At 13:00 the stated replay endpoint finds no ongoing no-rate interval. Splitting the increment
at rate boundaries does not itself supply the missing historical row or change that endpoint.
The set leaves unstated how this elapsed no-rate segment acquires the row/window the apportioning
reads. Funding's model excludes rate outages and establishes no historical replay behavior.

## Follow-up scope

Decide and specify the missing historical-row/replay behavior, then add conformance traces for
both writers and the matched stop-boundary variant. Any formal coverage must state its replay
and retention assumptions. This record selects no repair. Do not conflate it with live-opened
rows closing at rate return or exit, or with billable-span clipping: those are handled by the
pv-vwe.34 two-axis follow-up. Related records pv-gip.18, pv-gip.19, pv-gip.28 and pv-gip.6 cover
other replay, column-writer, parameter and return-instant questions.

title: A rate outage lifts a solvency halt already in force
description: From the Spec review of pv-gip.31 (b682c8a). The halt holds only while the check fails: 01-domain-model.md ~558 'Refused because a solvency or rate-availability gate is failing'; 04-api-contract.md ~251 'while LDG-20's solvency halt is in force'. Trace: a computed shortfall lies in the USD leg, so the halt is in force and invoices are cancelled; USD's window then yields no rate; LDG-40's amended row omits the USD leg, the valued terms pass, minting resumes and the deposit read stops reporting gate solvency. That is LDG-20's own case ('a customer could pay for a claim the operator had just computed it could not honour'), and starving one currency's window now lifts a declared halt. ADR-0029's 'A missing rate computes no such insolvency' is false when the insolvency was computed first; its accepted cost covers only shortfalls arising during the outage. Owner's decision: record it as a cost, or a pass with a leg omitted proves nothing, so the last computed verdict stands until every leg can be valued.
close_reason: Implemented and verified in bb6449c; completion evidence in comment

comments.author: master
comments.text:
Decided 2026-10-04 by the owner ("Accept"; fable, astra, sol in panel r10 the same): a pass with a
leg omitted proves nothing, so the last computed verdict stands until every leg can be valued. An
incomplete check can still start a halt when its valued terms are short (pv-gip.31); it can never
lift one: a halt in force lifts only on a check with every leg valued. Accepted cost: a shortfall
cured during an outage (a recorded payment, satoshis added) keeps top-ups halted until the rate
returns. Rejected: record the lift as a cost (reopens LDG-20's "a customer could pay for a claim the
operator had just computed it could not honour"; starving one currency's window would lift a halt).

title: An interrupted cancellation can reach operator retry before its fence exists
description:
# Owner clarification: retry after interruption before the cancellation fence

Found by Opus in Round 1 of rloop Run 20261004T232205.225230922Z-2186469 and independently verified by the Manager against 922ff45e5de6bc106368e98d344248f0736b023a. This is a behavioral and conformance gap, not a cosmetic comment request. The assigned closed beads stay closed; this follow-up does not reopen Q11/Q12 or select their replacement.

## Passages and trace

- `03-operation-lifecycle.md:315`, OPS-15: “At startup, before any claim, the engine MUST move every `running` operation to `needs_reconciliation`”. Interrupt a cancellation after claim but before its fence transaction; no fence was written and no provider call occurred.
- OPS-48 at `03-operation-lifecycle.md:1025` maps `needs_reconciliation` to `uncertain` with “**Stays set**”; its resolved `not_applied` row at 1028 maps to `stalled` with the same fence cell. OPS-31 provides `not_applied`: “the mutation took effect, so the operation settles `succeeded`; or it did not, so it settles `failed`” (`03-operation-lifecycle.md:1122`). For the interrupted pre-dispatch delete, no mutation took effect.
- API-64 at `04-api-contract.md:1014` admits the stalled retry “by a conditional write guarded on `(id, state = stalled)`” and enqueues a fresh delete attempt. Its origin is stamped `requested_by: operator` with non-null `episode_id` at 1029.
- LDG-62 at `12-billing-and-ledger.md:1766` admits the guarded extension on “`machines.destroy_committed IS NULL`”. With a null fence, active tenant, healthy account, available rate, sufficient funds and no solvency halt, the customer can extend before the retry worker's fence transaction. API-7 supplies no separate open-episode refusal on this extension path.
- OPS-41 step 2 at `03-operation-lifecycle.md:812` says retry bypasses the funding decision “regardless of the current rate or suspension”. If the episode remains open and the machine present, its step 1 does not abort. The retried worker can fence and delete without reconsidering the newly funded machine.
- This conflicts with OPS-42's ordering sentence: “Extension first: the worker's read sees the new commitment, `OPS-41` applies, and it makes no provider call at all.”

## Readings requiring the owner

1. OPS-48's “Stays set” asserts a fence is already present at uncertain/stalled. Then the interrupted-claim path needs a specified writer/ordering that establishes it, which the current startup and resolution rules do not provide.
2. The table preserves the actual value, including null on the interrupted-claim path. Then an API-64 retry can be unfenced and the unconditional retry funding bypass conflicts with extension-first safety.

These lead to different admissible extensions, retry outcomes and provider calls. No reading is selected by this issue. Do not repair this by silently narrowing OPS-15, weakening OPS-42, or assuming every stalled episode is already fenced.

Recommendation: the owner should explicitly define when deletion becomes committed on a never-fenced interrupted attempt and what happens when an extension wins before that commitment, preserving OPS-42's extension-first guarantee. Specify the relevant startup/resolution/retry ordering and refusal behavior. Then align the model and conformance with that decision; do not treat a model omission as evidence of impossibility.

## Model and check gap

`tools/formal/Provisiond/Fence.lean:957` Event has no interrupted-worker/startup transition and omits OPS-31 resolution events (the module documents the latter). `RetryFenceInv` at 1753 and `retry_has_episode_fence` at 1957 are proved over this smaller event set. The proof is valid for that model; it does not establish that the specified interrupted path is unreachable. The new Markdown note at `03-operation-lifecycle.md:918` needs this limit made explicit when the repair proceeds. Current Init and transitions were unchanged by 922ff45.

CNF-271 at `10-conformance-checklist.md:1635` starts with a provider call that “fails after the fence is written”. It does not exercise interruption before fencing. After clarification, require a discriminating interruption -> startup -> resolution -> retry case, including extension before the retry worker and the opposing transaction order. The relevant model/negative-control evidence must reject the violating trace, not merely compile a model excluding it.

## Acceptance

Obtain an owner decision with the quoted passages and both readings visible; land the rule at its owner, preserve closed decisions outside this clarification, align affected Lean declarations without assumed fence premises, disclose model limits, and add conformance that fails the bad interrupted path. Run required gates and affected in-place negative controls. No fix is authorized or attempted by this issue's creation.

Run report: `.rloop/runs/20261004T232205.225230922Z-2186469/finished.md`. Base: 62dcfd248f4182cda83cc4c3538928b880a17178. Model/spec repair commit: 922ff45e5de6bc106368e98d344248f0736b023a.

Home: OPS-41 step 2. The suspension half of step 2 stays unconditional. title: ADR-0028 in the requirements: the restore grace is one instant in the restore record; destroy_not_before withdrawn
description:
## Parent

`pv-gip`. This ticket lands `ADR-0028` (2026-09-25, amended the same day after a four-reader
self-consistency pass) in the requirements: the restore grace becomes one instant in the restore
record, and `machines.destroy_not_before` is withdrawn. `pv-gip.2` then models what the text says
(`ADR-0025`), so wording here is load-bearing. `ADR-0028`'s Consequences section is the edit list;
this ticket names the same edits and no others.

## What to land

Each bullet names the owner of a rule; everywhere else points at it (`AGENTS.md`). Every sentence
asserting what another requirement says carries that requirement's words. Every withdrawn rule
carries a dated 2026-09-25 note in the house form, after the record it amends, retaining the
withdrawn wording where a trap sits behind it — and the per-machine deadline is such a trap: it
looked right, was built for two days, and produced the five defects the ADR lists.

- **`STO-56`** gains `grace_ends_at`, nullable, written in the same transaction as step (3)'s
  mark ("A marked step does not run again") as that instant plus one re-derivation interval; and
  the rule that the record MUST NOT be closed before `grace_ends_at` has passed. Its existing
  sentence about both components reading the open row first is the startup read and does not
  cover the per-claim read, which `OPS-41` owns.
- **`STO-54`**: the freeze on the five frozen actors lifts at `grace_ends_at` rather than "when
  step (3) completes" (the `suspend_tenant` exception's own later condition stands on top); the
  step (1) clause writing `destroy_not_before` on "every machine whose stored `runway_until` has
  passed" is withdrawn; the "what the restore does not repair" paragraph says the grace is one
  interval from step (3), that a machine whose fence is set gets no extension from it — its route
  back is `OPS-42`'s — and that a retry's claim waits the interval like every claim. Quote
  `ADR-0028` for the reason, once.
- **`OPS-41`**: the claim rule — a claim of an exposure-reducing cancellation MUST defer while a
  restore record is open and its `grace_ends_at` is null or in the future: to `grace_ends_at` when
  it is set, by `OPS-8`'s short delay when it is not yet written; "the same write as `OPS-8`'s
  defer, though nothing refused it" (`F51`'s words — cite `F51`, since `OPS-8` covers an index
  refusal and a short delay, and this rule states its own scope and duration); the worker reads
  the restore record at each such claim; the rule applies whichever path enqueued the
  cancellation. Nothing in `OPS-41` reads `destroy_not_before` today; the provider-call sentence
  is `LDG-16`'s, below.
- **`LDG-16`**: the deadline paragraph withdrawn, including the sentence `pv-gip.1` gave it — "an
  exposure-reducing cancellation MUST NOT make its provider call while its machine's
  `destroy_not_before` is in the future" — retained in the dated note as the trap; the routing
  predicate is "stored `runway_until` has passed" alone; the bypass sentence says the bound's and
  the suspended tenant's cancellations claim like every other and wait for the grace; the worker
  sentences become one — the worker reads no fact the grace wrote.
- **`LDG-62`**, **`OPS-41`**: "clears the deadline" withdrawn where it survives from pv-gip.1.
- **`LDG-65`**: its deadline clause withdrawn; the outage-expiry and bound cases claim like every
  other. **`LDG-64`** carries no deadline sentence and is not touched.
- **`PRV-13e`**: "never writes `machines.destroy_not_before`" withdrawn.
- **`05-persistence.md`** machines table: the `destroy_not_before` row withdrawn with a dated note
  in the row's place per README's conventions; `STO-49`/`STO-54` cross-references that name it
  follow.
- **`CNF-99`**'s restore cases: measured from step (3); a queued delete re-run after a restore and
  claimed before step (3) defers by a short delay and writes no fence; one claimed after step (3)
  is re-queued to `grace_ends_at` and writes no fence; an extension inside the grace closes the
  episode `funded` at the re-claim; a fenced machine gets no extension.
- **`CNF-295`**'s restore rehearsal: its two assertions of `destroy_not_before` become assertions
  of `grace_ends_at` on the record.
- **`CONTEXT.md`** already carries **Restore grace**; if the rule and the glossary disagree, the
  rule is wrong.

## Must not touch

`LDG-38`, `LDG-58`, `LDG-59`, `STO-37` (the window and the opener are `ADR-0027`'s and are done or
in `pv-gip.16`'s hands). `tools/` and `docs/adr/` beyond a citation. `OPS-48`'s table gains no row:
a re-queued attempt has not settled.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `grep -n "destroy_not_before" *.md` finds only dated withdrawal notes
- [ ] `grep -n "reads neither fact\|destruction deadline\|MUST NOT make its provider call" 12-billing-and-ledger.md` finds only dated notes
- [ ] `OPS-41` carries the claim rule with both branches (null, future) and the per-claim read;
      `STO-56` carries `grace_ends_at` and the closure rule
- [ ] `CNF-99` carries the five restore cases; `CNF-295` asserts the record, not the column
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, unpiped
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes

title: LDG-64 closes the absorbed window at observed_at while STO-49 lets a pass read early and commit late
description:
## Parent

`pv-gip` — the window median (`ADR-0027`). Raised by `gpt-5.6-sol` reviewing `pv-gip.1`
(2026-09-23). Pre-existing: the same instant was the closer before `ADR-0027`.

## The gap

`LDG-64` closes the absorbed window "with that observation's instant" — its `observed_at`.
`STO-49` says a row is "written before that rate is used for anything" and that "a pass that reads
early and commits late, writes a row whose instant precedes one already stored". A row observed at
`t0` and accepted at `t1` ends the outage at `t0`, though no rate was usable until `t1`; the
hours `t0..t1` are then priced at a rate that did not exist while they elapsed — what `LDG-64`'s
"never billed retroactively" forbids.

## Recommendation

Close the absorbed window at the accepting write's instant (or the later of the two), stated in
`LDG-64`, and say in `STO-49` which column carries it if `observed_at` cannot.
close_reason: Q13 and residue completed together in 88503f7

comments.author: master
comments.text: Q13 decided 2026-10-04 by the owner ("agree"), panel r16 (/var/tmp/provisiond-panel-r16/synthesis.md; astra, sol, opus for; fable for redefining observed_at instead): STO-49 gains accepted_at, set to max(the clock in the accepting transaction, the previous row's accepted_at for that currency) in the transaction that allocates acceptance_order, so time order and acceptance order cannot disagree. Every pass verdict takes effect at its row's accepted_at: LDG-38's increment split, LDG-64's return, STO-37's thin start, LDG-58's latest pass as of an instant, OPS-41's paused-measure spans. Staleness stays observed_at plus the row's stamped bound (a price's age is the evidence's age), counting only rows accepted by that instant, so a late row can only end an outage at its acceptance and never moves a past start. The absorbed window closes at max(accepted_at, the subject's mark), so absorbed_seconds equals the relief actually given. Home: LDG-58 (the verdict's owner). further than to a neighbouring price some honest pass in the window accepted" — `LDG-16`

title: The Lean pass of the citation gate has no document pool
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`).

## The gap

`pv-vwe.18` gave the QUOTED rule a second source, the Lean docstrings under `tools/formal/`, and
passes them to `find()` as their own dict. `find()`'s document pool at the `docpool` line resolves a
`` `NN-name.md` `` citation against **the dict it was handed**. For the Lean pass that dict holds
only `.lean` keys, so `docpool` is always empty: a docstring that quotes a document's own words and
names the document cannot verify against it.

Nine such document citations already sit inside Lean docstrings — `Admission.lean`, `Claim.lean`,
`Fence.lean` (`05-persistence.md`), `Rescue.lean` (`01-domain-model.md`, `05-persistence.md`,
`CONTEXT.md`). None fires today, because none of them also carries an attribution verb and a quote.
The first docstring that does will be a false positive no baseline anticipated, and the reader will
be told a correct quote is unverifiable.

## Shape

Give `find()` the Markdown `docs` as its document pool independently of the dict being scanned — a
third parameter, or a separate lookup dict — so the Lean pass resolves `` `NN-name.md` `` the way
the Markdown pass does. Add a docstring that quotes a document's own words as the regression check.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Lean docstring quoting a document's own words alongside its filename verifies
- [ ] The three baselined residue spans are unchanged; no new baseline entry
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green

title: QUOTED loses trailing possessive apostrophes during nested-quote normalization
description:
Found during Round 2 acceptance of the citation repair, after a2b58e458f856c9b6e8735df07455f3b0029e2c0. Fable and Opus noted the remaining case; the Manager independently reproduced it with the real requirement corpus. This is a check-detection follow-up, not a cosmetic documentation request. The scoped word-internal-apostrophe repair is accepted; neither pv-n9p nor pv-vwe.35 is reopened.

LDG-57 in 12-billing-and-ledger.md says "A deployment MUST watch only unexpired deposits' addresses". A current attribution `LDG-57` says "A deployment MUST watch only unexpired deposits addresses". is compared but incorrectly accepted. The only alteration removes the trailing possessive apostrophe.

Read-only reproduction from the repository root:

```python
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, 'tools')
import check_citations as c
docs, adrs, reqs = c.load()
text = '`LDG-57` says "A deployment MUST watch only unexpired deposits addresses".'
print(c.find({'probe.md': text}, adrs, reqs))
```

At a2b58e4 the result is ([], [], 1). Loading tools/check_citations.py from git show d9d68b6:tools/check_citations.py into a module and running the same find() over the current corpus gives one LDG-57 finding: a deployment must watch only unexpired deposits addresses. Synthetic rows' / rows probes also match incorrectly in both directions.

Cause: QUOTED comparison_text preserves single marks only between word characters; a trailing possessive mark is removed like a closing quotation delimiter. Its current docstring accurately states that narrow rule. EXISTS intentionally retains its older removal of all single and double marks and is not the subject of this report.

Follow-up should distinguish trailing possessive content from nested quotation delimiters sufficiently to reject this misquote while preserving the accepted nested-quotation match, word-internal apostrophe protection, and baseline identities. Assess the appropriate bounded comparison behavior before implementation; no algorithm is selected here. Demonstrate exact -> named QUOTED failure -> restored exact on the real gate and a control that fails when the protection is removed. Do not broaden baseline exemptions or rewrite historical records to hide the case. This issue was filed only, not selected or worked in the repair Run.
close_reason: Stopped after Round 4 by the owner's session (review ratchet). Kept Rounds 1-3 (34d347b..c23c2d2): trailing and independent possessives, delimiter equivalence, complete pairs across elisions and shared edges. Reverted Round 4's tools/check_citations.py and ci.yml (b7a867c) to the Round-3 versions: its itertools.product search over per-fragment occurrences is exponential (a real-corpus quote 'A deployment … MUST … only … deposits addresses' took 39 s; Round 3: 0.28 s, correct named finding; the exact form passes in 0.23 s). Full gates and both citation negative controls pass on the restored code. Round 4's R7/R8 cases are filed as the follow-up.

title: The citation gate does not check a quote attributed by a bare possessive
description:
Raised by the opus Reviewer of the pv-vwe.30 / pv-vwe.27 Run, 2026-10-02, by running the gate's own `find()`.

## What was found

`tools/check_citations.py`'s `ATTRIB` matches a speech verb ("`X` says …") or the possessive-noun
form ("`X`'s rule that …"). A possessive followed directly by a quote — `` `LDG-72`'s "the greatest
`increment end` among that subject's rows" `` — matches neither, so the quote is not checked.
Reproduced on `CNF-216`'s 2026-10-02 clause: with "greatest" changed to "smallest" the gate stays
green; the same misquote behind "`LDG-72` says" is refused. The shape is what the Run's briefs
recommend for long sentences, and it already occurs across `11-open-findings.md`, `02-`, `05-`,
`13-` and the ADRs, so those quotes rest on hand checks only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A quote of four or more words directly after `` `X`'s `` is checked against X's body, or the
      gate's docstring names the shape under "what this does not catch" with the reason
- [ ] If checked: a negative control (a misquote in that shape is red), and the standing residue
      ratcheted rather than failed outright

```python
import sys,re,json,subprocess
sys.path.insert(0,'tools')
import types,os
rev='85ae85856fe6494cc0d5fb80f5e48613727fe83a'
c=types.ModuleType('citations_at_first_closure')
c.__file__=os.path.abspath('tools/check_citations.py')
exec(subprocess.check_output(['git','show',rev+':tools/check_citations.py'],text=True), c.__dict__)
bare=re.compile(r'`((?:%s)-\d+[a-z]?)`\'s\s+(?=["“])' % c.NS)

def measure(texts,docs,adrs,reqs):
 rows=[]; skipped=[]
 for f,t in texts.items():
  for sent in c.chunks(t):
   quotes=dict(c.quotations(sent))
   for m in bare.finditer(sent):
    if m.end() not in quotes: continue
    rid=m.group(1); quote=c.norm(quotes[m.end()])
    pool=([c.norm(reqs[rid][1])] if rid in reqs else [])
    pool += [c.norm(docs[d]) for d in c.DOC.findall(sent) if d in docs]
    pool += [c.norm(adrs[a]) for a in c.ADR.findall(sent) if a in adrs]
    row=dict(file=f,attribution=rid,quote=quote,
       source_file=reqs.get(rid,('MISSING',''))[0],
       verified=any(all(fr in p for fr in c.fragments(quote)) for p in pool))
    if c.HISTORICAL.search(sent) or c.TEACHING.search(sent): skipped.append(row)
    else: rows.append(row)
 return dict(compared=len(rows),findings=[r for r in rows if not r['verified']],rows=rows,skipped=skipped)

if __name__=='__main__':

```

title: check_citations.py's sentence splitter does not break on a sentence that ends inside markup
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`).

## The defect

`tools/check_citations.py`'s `SPLIT` is

    re.compile(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+|\n\s*[-*]\s+|\n\s*\n|\n(?=\|)")

The lookbehind wants the character immediately before the whitespace to be a sentence ender. It is
not, whenever the sentence closes inside markup: `happen.**"` ends with `"`, `it does.*` ends with
`*`, `` runs.` `` ends with a backtick. Those sentences do not break, so one chunk carries an
attribution verb for one requirement and then a later citation's quote, and `find()` blames the
verb's requirement for words it does not contain.

## Measured

One entry in `tools/citation-baseline.json`'s `quoted_attributions` is this defect.
`tools/formal/Provisiond/Admission.lean:603-605`:

> `LDG-62` grows the commitment "from available balance at the **current** rate", and `LDG-59` says
> "**Falling back to the last known rate MUST NOT happen.**" A purchase priced at an unknown rate is
> what create's row halts for, and the extension is "authorized like a purchase".

The sentence closes at `happen.**"`; the lookbehind sees `"` and does not fire; `LDG-62`'s
"authorized like a purchase" lands in `LDG-59`'s chunk and is reported against `LDG-59`.

**The other two entries are NOT this defect** and this ticket does not retire them. The two spans
blamed on `LDG-40` at `Admission.lean:773-776` are one English sentence whose only `.` is its last
character; there is no sentence ending inside it for any lookbehind to miss. Their cause is
`find()`'s `owner = rid` — one attribution verb owns every quote in its chunk — over a single
sentence citing two requirements. Widening the ownership rule was considered for `pv-vwe.18` and
rejected: it reintroduces the inverted-attribution class `find()`'s own comment records
("`STO-43` says `STO-14` 'reaches settled operations'" is STO-43's sentence *about* STO-14).
Those two have no exit today, by decision.

## Shape

Widen the lookbehind to allow closing markup between the sentence ender and the whitespace —
`(?<=[.!?])[*`"”)\]]*\s+` or equivalent — and re-run. The Markdown surface is clean under the
current splitter, so any change there is a regression; check it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `SPLIT` breaks a sentence that ends inside closing markup
- [ ] Every `*.md` still clean; the `--selftest` WIR-1 known-positive still fires
- [ ] The `LDG-59` entry is gone from `citation-baseline.json`'s `quoted_attributions`; the note
      no longer names this ticket as the two `LDG-40` entries' exit
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green

title: A stale citation-baseline entry is green; the ratchet enforces only one direction
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`).

## The gap

Both baselines in `tools/citation-baseline.json` say "may shrink, never grow", and the gate enforces
only the second half. Nothing makes a **stale** entry red:

- when `pv-split-lookbehind-markup-ch2` retires the `LDG-59` span, its `quoted_attributions` entry
  stays and the gate stays green;
- if `tools/formal/` moves or is renamed, `load_lean_docstrings()` returns `{}` silently and every
  baselined signature goes unmatched — the whole Lean surface stops being checked with no red.

Both print a visible mismatch (`Lean quoted attributions: 2, none new against baseline 3`) and
neither fails. `check_citations.py`'s own docstring already holds the standard this falls short of,
for the index: "a missing index is a red gate, not a skipped rule."

The `unquoted_attributions` baseline has the same gap, so this is a widening rather than a
correction, which is why it was not folded into `pv-vwe.18`.

## Shape

Fail when a baselined signature is not among the current findings, for both baselines, naming the
entry to delete. That makes "may shrink, never grow" a thing the gate enforces instead of a thing
the note asserts, and gives the silent-skip case the treatment a missing index already gets.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A baselined signature that no longer fires makes the gate exit 1 and names the stale entry
- [ ] Emptying `tools/formal/` of `.lean` files is red, not green
- [ ] HEAD is green with no stale entries in either baseline
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green

## A third case, found 2026-09-22

The bootstrap at the end of `main()` still rewrites `citation-baseline.json` from scratch when
`["unquoted_attributions"]` raises, and the dict it writes carries only `unquoted_attributions` and
the pre-Lean note — it would silently drop `quoted_attributions`. `pv-vwe.18` established that this
path is unreachable while the three Lean residue findings exist, but that argument is conditional on
the quoted half being clean, which a hand-edited baseline missing only the unquoted key satisfies.
The damage is loud rather than silent (the next run goes red with three findings) and the trigger
needs a hand-mangled file, which is why it is filed here rather than fixed in `pv-vwe.18`.

- [ ] The bootstrap preserves `quoted_attributions`, or refuses to run while it is non-empty

title: An unterminated Lean block comment leaves the citation gate through a traceback
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`).

## The gap

`docstrings()` raises `ValueError('unterminated Lean block comment')` and `load_lean_docstrings()`
does not catch it, so a `.lean` file whose block comment never closes leaves the gate through a
traceback rather than through its own voice:

```
File ".../check_citations.py", line 194, in load_lean_docstrings
    docs[...] = '\n\n'.join(docstrings(source.read()))
ValueError: unterminated Lean block comment
exit=1
```

The message does not name the file, although `load_lean_docstrings()` has the path in hand. It is the
one extractor failure mode that does not behave like the others: every other case prints
`FAIL: <case>` and returns 1.

Low reach: Lean rejects an unterminated block comment, and `check_formal.sh` runs before this gate in
`check-all.sh`, so the build is already red by the time the citations gate runs. It bites someone
running `python3 tools/check_citations.py` on its own.

`pv-vwe.18` verified and shipped this path as-is; it predates that ticket's own extractor work.

## Two prose items to fold in while touching that docstring

One rule, one home, so these are recorded here rather than as tickets of their own.

- The exit line reads "an unverifiable quote, an unresolved name or a rise above the baseline or a
  failed extractor case". Two `or`s invite reading the last two as a pair; a comma after "name" fixes
  it.
- "A failed extractor case" has no referent above it: nothing in the module docstring mentions the
  fixture table, so a reader must find `check_docstrings()` to learn what a case is. Half a clause in
  the QUOTED paragraph, which already owns the Lean pass, would give it a home.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An unterminated block comment under `tools/formal/` produces a gate message naming the file, and
      the exit code the module docstring claims for it
- [ ] The exit line's two prose items above are folded in
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green

title: The formal layer: every clause in the inventory gets a Lean home (ADR-0025, M2 through M8)
description:
## Problem Statement

The specification set has 497 requirements, six specification gates and a habit of cross-model review, and on 2026-09-12 three defects still landed that every gate and two readers passed: each citation resolved while the consequences contradicted. `LDG-38` described its billing-period reset as the customer's favour when the arithmetic says the opposite; `STO-12` and `STO-13` together demanded something PostgreSQL refuses; `STO-54` and `ADR-0023` called a one-interval grace a repair. The gates check that a rule is cited, owned and phrased; nothing checks what a rule implies, and the one gate that executed anything sampled floating-point inputs and never crossed a period boundary.

The owner's decision (`ADR-0025`) is that the set's precise semantics — calculations, predicates, closed tables and the lifecycle transitions with their real transaction and provider-call boundaries — are carried in Lean under `tools/formal/`, proved for every input, with the historical defects retained as executable witnesses so that "a plausible but incorrect amendment can no longer pass review merely because its prose sounds consistent". The first milestone (arithmetic and witnesses) has landed, been reviewed and been fixed. This spec is the remaining inventory.

## Solution

Extend the formal layer milestone by milestone until every clause in the agreed inventory has a Lean home: the claim model, the cancellation fence composed on it, the closed tables with the rendering gate that keeps the Markdown honest, reconciliation knowledge and restore, funding and the tenant lifecycle, rescue and install, wire canonicalization and redaction. Each milestone lands as theorems over every input, decided witnesses for the historical defects, and a negative theorem for every guard a dated amendment added — refused with the guard, admitted without it — all behind the one specification gate the set already runs, with a CI negative control per check.

Authority follows `ADR-0025`: a formalized clause's home is its tagged declaration; the requirement keeps its identifier, MUST, rationale and retained traps; the rendered formula or table is generated or diffed, never trusted. A theorem is never a conformance item.

## User Stories

1. As a spec author, I want a rule I amend to break a theorem when the amendment contradicts a property the set claims, so that the contradiction is found before review rather than by it.
2. As a spec author, I want the historical defects (`usable_sats > 0`, per-tick rounding, the unfenced funding read, the missing claim term, the period-reset direction) kept as executable witnesses, so that none can be re-laid without a red build.
3. As a spec author, I want every guard a dated amendment added to be a parameter of the model that carries it, so that removing the guard is a one-token change a witness theorem exercises.
4. As a spec author, I want a formalized formula or table rendered into the requirement from its declaration, so that I never maintain two copies by hand.
5. As a spec author, I want a rendered region that carries prose or citations diffed rather than rewritten, so that the rationale and citations around a table survive regeneration.
6. As a spec author, I want a backticked declaration name in a document to be checked against the emitted index, so that a renamed declaration cannot leave a dangling citation.
7. As a spec author, I want the model's identities (`OperationId`, `ClaimNumber`, `EpisodeId`, `MachineId`, `TenantId`) to be distinct types, so that a fence holding an attempt's id instead of an episode's is a type error rather than a review finding.
8. As a spec author, I want "the store committed" and "the worker learned it committed" to be separate facts in the model, so that `ADR-0022`'s lost reply is representable and not collapsed into rollback.
9. As a spec author, I want "dispatched", "applied" and "response received" to be separate facts for a provider call, so that a lost response is never read as evidence nothing happened.
10. As a spec author, I want `OPS-49`'s "never the last failed statement" to be a refuted alternative in the model, so that the prohibited partial-statement retry is expressible and shown harmful.
11. As a spec author, I want both commit orderings of `OPS-42`'s fence proved, so that "one of them provably loses" is a theorem and not a sentence.
12. As a spec author, I want the cancellation model to carry the rate-outage branch, the tenant's current suspension state and the episode, so that the theorem proved is about the requirement as written and not a simplification of it.
13. As a spec author, I want `OPS-33`'s release-without-resolution to be a reachable positive witness (`unknown` knowledge with a closed commitment), so that the model cannot mistake release for absence.
14. As a spec author, I want absence evidence to require a complete pass, an elapsed window and a direct reread as three separate conjuncts, so that dropping any one admits a witness.
15. As a spec author, I want restart and restore to be distinct events with distinct trace types, so that a restart theorem cannot be cited as covering a restore.
16. As a spec author, I want `STO-54`'s "an extension lost in Δ is not rebuilt" to be a proved existential, so that the weaker recovery guarantee is stated by a theorem and not assumed away.
17. As a spec author, I want every closed table (`OPS-11`, `OPS-3`, `OPS-48`, `DOM-31`, the halt matrix) to be a total function whose totality is decided, so that adding a kind without a row fails the build.
18. As a spec author, I want a migration plan's transaction mode to be a type, so that `F52`'s second defect — a `CONCURRENTLY` build inside a transaction — cannot be written.
19. As a spec author, I want the ledger's "consumption leaves `available` unchanged" and the clamp's "the credit is untouched" proved over every input, so that the 2026-09-02 double charge is unrepresentable.
20. As a spec author, I want provider windows, PostgreSQL semantics and `OPS-47`'s single engine to appear as named hypotheses on the theorems that depend on them, so that a signature shows what was assumed.
21. As a reviewer reading a landing without memory of the session, I want the emitted index to say which requirement each declaration formalizes, so that I can check a declaration against the sentence it claims to carry.
22. As a reviewer, I want every proof to rest on the three standard axioms only, with `sorry`, project axioms and `native_decide` refused by the gate, so that a green build means what it says.
23. As a reviewer, I want each new check to have a CI control that breaks the thing it guards and asserts the failure came from that check, so that a red for the wrong reason is never taken as evidence.
24. As CI, I want the formal layer to build and gate in the same job as the textual gates, under the same Nix shell a developer uses, so that there is one toolchain definition.
25. As CI, I want a module the build never imports to be refused, so that a proof file nobody reads is not a green check.
26. As a future implementer, I want the model's definitions to compute permitted outcomes for a sequence of commands and faults, so that an implementation can be compared against them in a test, without that comparison being mistaken for a refinement proof.
27. As a future implementer, I want the conformance checklist to count nothing from the formal layer, so that a proved model never reads as a passed test.
28. As the owner, I want the inventory built in the order that lets each model be true when it lands — claim before fence, tables before the rendering gate, reconciliation and restore before funding — so that no milestone proves a false requirement to save time.
29. As the owner, I want Mathlib added only in a commit naming the theorem that cannot close without it, so that the dependency is never carried by default.
30. As the owner, I want the glossary term **reference model** added when the first lifecycle model exists, so that the glossary never describes an artifact that does not exist.

## Implementation Decisions

**Order and milestones.** Each milestone is one ticket; a milestone's acceptance is a proof or decided check that fails on a named historical defect.

- M2, the claim model (`ADR-0022`, `OPS-5`, `OPS-6`, `OPS-8`, `OPS-22`, `OPS-49`, `STO-3`). A durable row with status and claim number; executions each holding their claim; a transaction as a list of statements with the guarded status write first; whole-transaction restart as the retry, with the last-statement retry definable so it can be refuted; the store outcome as committed-and-acked pairs; the provider outcome as dispatched, applied, reply. Theorems: a stale execution's write is inert after a later claim; a same-claim repetition changes nothing, `revision` included; provider calls across store retries are at most one; a lost reply on the claim itself is a transition to exit and never a re-claim. Witness pair: the stale-defer trace refused with the claim term, admitted without it. Both panel readers proved that pair in scratch; the decision-rich shape, from that prototype:

  ```
  guardOk withClaimTerm row write := row.status = running ∧ (¬withClaimTerm ∨ row.claim = write.mine)
  trace withClaimTerm := A claims (1); A defers; reply lost; B claims (2); A repeats its defer
  refused  : (trace true).status  = running
  admitted : (trace false).status = queued
  ```

- M3, the cancellation fence composed on M2 (`OPS-41`, `OPS-42`, `LDG-62`, `OPS-48`, `LDG-16`, `ADR-0021`). Model state carries the machine's commitment, stored date and `exhausted_since`, the fence as an optional episode id, the episode and its state, the rate as optional (outage is a branch, not a value), the tenant's current suspension state, and time. Events: sweep routing on the stored date and the column, claim, the fence transaction with its re-check inside it as a parameter, extension in its own serialization guarded on the fence, provider delete outside the serialization, reply, settlement, gone-write, retry from stalled only, rate movement. Invariants over reachable states with the single-engine assumption in the signature: destruction only after a fence transaction whose re-check read unfunded, no rate, or suspended; an extension after the fence opens nothing and moves nothing; an extension before the fence is seen by the re-check; a set fence names an open episode with the same id; closed is absorbing; gone clears the fence and closes the episode together. Witnesses, one parameter each: re-check outside the fence transaction, fence holding the attempt id, the withdrawn abort predicate inside the lifecycle, abort without the date write, suspension keyed on episode reasons.

- M4, the closed tables and the rendering gate (`OPS-11`, `OPS-3`, `OPS-48`, `DOM-31`, `DOM-17`). Each table is a total function with a `match` carrying no wildcard, its totality decided. The rendering gate: `lake exe gate` already emits the index; a Python specification gate reads it, diffs every marked region in the documents against what the declaration emits, generates the pure-computation regions, and resolves every backticked declaration name. The citations gate gains that resolver. `check-all.sh` orders the formal build before the gates that read its index. First marked regions: `OPS-48`'s transition table and `DOM-31`'s diagram emitted and diffed; `LDG-38`'s worked examples and `LDG-31`'s worked table generated. The migration-plan type (transactional versus standalone statement) lands here as the formal home of `F52`'s second defect.

- M5, reconciliation knowledge and restore (`OPS-32`, `OPS-33`, `OPS-36`, `OPS-27`, `PRV-36`, `STO-54`, `STO-5`, `OPS-15`). Knowledge as `unknown`, `observed present`, `authoritative absence`, `multiple candidates`, separate from the commitment's open or closed; absence evidence as three conjuncts; two window fields, never one. Fault events `crash`, `restart`, `restore Δ`, `complete procedure` with separate trace types; recovery phases as separate permissions, never one Boolean; quarantine of the irreversible kinds before the first claim; the lost extension not rebuilt as a proved existential.

- M6, funding and the tenant lifecycle (`LDG-8`, `LDG-9`, `LDG-31`, `LDG-70`, `STO-30`, `STO-31`, `WIR-42`, `API-34`, `API-35`). Ledger conservation; the clamp and the deficiency as separate quantities in separate units; rail-identity replay; deposit expiry; tenant deletion; operator attribution.

- M7, rescue and install (`RSC-3`–`RSC-5`, `RSC-26`, `RSC-39`–`RSC-44`, `OPS-45`). Trust state, inventory validation, write-started markers, rescue exit, recovery-key retention. Physical and cryptographic facts are hypotheses.

- M8, wire canonicalization, redaction and admission (`API-9`, `API-12`, `WIR-1a`, `WIR-32`, `API-21`, `STO-50`, `API-7`, `SEC-39`, `LDG-20`, `LDG-40`). Canonical serialization, fingerprint preimage, projection and redaction idempotence, the admission and halt matrices as decided policy spaces. Whether `WIR-37`'s fixtures are generated is decided at the end of M4 on the evidence of the rendering mechanism; if yes, `13-wire-contract.md`'s precedence sentence is amended to say a registered shape renders its declaration.

**Authority and rendering** (`ADR-0025`). One declaration per formalized clause, tagged with the requirement identifier; the requirement keeps identifier, MUST, rationale, amendment record and traps. Until a clause's region is gated, the Markdown is authoritative and the Lean is a checking interpretation. Ids stay append-only; withdrawn definitions live in a historical namespace that current policy cannot select. No hand-kept manifest.

**Trust.** Standard three axioms only, `sorryAx` refused transitively, no project axioms, `native_decide` refused everywhere under the project namespace except an `Explore` namespace nothing tags or cites. Rational witnesses close by `decide +kernel`. No Mathlib unless a named theorem cannot close without it.

**Assumptions.** Provider behaviour, PostgreSQL semantics and the single engine are named hypotheses on the theorems that use them; a model that omits a second engine says so in its docstring. Never an `axiom`.

**Vocabulary.** Specification gate, witness, model, assumption, property as defined in the glossary. **Reference model** is added to the glossary with M2, the first lifecycle model. *Oracle* stays banned. A settlement parameter is never named *target*.

**Modules.** One module per model, shared identity and outcome types in one place, witnesses in one module, the gate executable unchanged in role. Every module imported by the root, which the wrapper enforces.

## Testing Decisions

- The seam is `check-all.sh`: `lake build`, `lake exe gate`, the Python gates. Nothing else tests the formal layer.
- A good test is a property of external behaviour: a theorem about what the definitions imply for every input, or a decided witness over a concrete trace. Never a test of a proof's internals or a tactic's shape.
- Every guard has its pair: refused with the guard, admitted without. A model with only the positive theorem is incomplete.
- Every model has a successful execution witness (a create that succeeds, a cancellation that destroys) so that a model that refuses everything cannot satisfy its safety theorems vacuously.
- Every new check gets a CI negative control that mutates the thing the check guards, asserts the build or gate went red, and asserts the red came from that check and not from a syntax error or a missing toolchain. `ci.yml` holds the list. Prior art: the four Lean controls and the four textual controls already there.
- Bounded exploration publishes its bounds; it is evidence within them and not an unbounded theorem.
- A theorem never counts toward conformance coverage; the coverage gate reads nothing from the formal layer.

## Out of Scope

- An implementation oracle or a refinement proof; comparing a future implementation to the model is a test, and building that comparison waits for an implementation.
- Aeneas, Verso, or any documentation-platform migration.
- Formalizing provider behaviour, PostgreSQL, deployment, cryptographic hardness, or legal and commercial obligations beyond naming them as hypotheses.
- Rewriting the textual Python gates in Lean.
- Telling tenants a restore interval is running (decided against, `STO-54`).
- Wire fixture generation until M4's evidence is in.

## Further Notes

The panel that shaped this — Codex at xhigh and a fresh Fable reader on one brief — both warned that the fence model built without the claim model, the rate-outage branch, the suspended-tenant branch and the episode proves a false requirement; M3 depends on M2 for that reason and not for convenience. The same panel found by running Lean that `decide` sticks on rational equalities and that `decide +kernel` closes them under the standard axioms; that is why the trust policy can refuse `native_decide` outright.

This set's own record is that each fix round introduces defects at about the rate it removes them and that green gates are not the check. Every milestone therefore ends with a two-axis review of its diff before the next begins.

title: Claim model: shared identity and outcome types, ADR-0022's guard theorems
description:
## Parent

pv-vwe — the formal layer, M2 through M8 (`ADR-0025`).

## What to build

The first lifecycle model. Distinct types for `OperationId`, `ClaimNumber`, `EpisodeId`, `MachineId`, `TenantId` (structures, never aliases); a store outcome as committed-and-acked, a provider outcome as dispatched, applied, reply. A durable row with status and claim number; executions each holding their claim; a transaction as a list of statements whose guarded status write comes first; whole-transaction restart as the retry, with the last-statement retry definable so `OPS-49`'s prohibition can be refuted rather than assumed. Every guard `STO-3` states is a parameter. Prototype shape, from the panel's probe: `guardOk withClaimTerm row write := row.status = running ∧ (¬withClaimTerm ∨ row.claim = write.mine)`; trace: A claims (1), A defers, reply lost, B claims (2), A repeats its defer. title: ADR-0026: the exhaustion mark becomes two facts, in the requirements
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`). The decision is `ADR-0026`.

## What to land

`ADR-0026`'s two facts, in the Markdown. The ADR holds the argument and the rejected alternatives;
this ticket writes the rules.

- **`LDG-16`** — replace the one setter and one clearer with the two facts. The rate confirmation
  reference is armed by **every rate-produced backward move**; where one write both arms it and
  lands in the future, **the arm wins**. It is discharged only by a strictly later accepted
  observation: still-exhausted confirms and permits routing, future-dated writes that date and
  clears. The wait is no longer "older than one re-derivation interval". Narrow the requirement's
  claim to **transient** error, per the ADR's "What this does not promise".
- **`PRV-13e`** — re-derivation arms the reference and records which observation it consumed.
- **`LDG-65`** — the outage rule keys on the new fact; `LDG-64`'s bound bypasses confirmation, since
  the deployment must "**cancel machines at that bound** if no rate has returned" and no observation
  will arrive to discharge anything.
- **`STO-54`** — the restore writes the **deadline**, not the rate reference, and preserves any
  reference already present. Its grace "buys the tenant one re-derivation interval in which to
  extend again" and no observation discharges it.
- **`STO-49`** — a transactionally increasing per-currency **acceptance order**. The table is
  "unique on `(currency, observed_at)`" and nothing makes `observed_at` monotone or non-reusable, so
  the comparison cannot be a timestamp. Retention must cover a referenced observation, which today
  is stated only in terms of subjects with an open increment.
- **`05-persistence.md`** — two columns where there was one, the reference written in the same
  transaction as the date it explains.
- **`OPS-41`** — the suspended-tenant path keeps its existing bypass; the ADR quotes it.
- **`CNF-99`** — drop the forty-five-to-forty case the wider arming rule deliberately changes; add
  the reading that crosses the horizon backward and lands in the future, which is the input that
  would have caught the dead branch; keep the natural-expiry and restore assertions unchanged.

## What must not change

`LDG-16`'s natural-expiry behaviour. Its own sentence is the reason the universal fence was
rejected: "The null case routes immediately, and that is the point: natural expiry of a runway the
customer was shown is not a glitch, and delaying it an interval would run every ordinary exhaustion
one interval into the wind-down reserve this requirement exists to keep whole."

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each requirement above amended, `ADR-0026` cited where the argument lives, with the withdrawn
      wording retained only where a trap sits behind it (`README.md`'s retention convention)
- [ ] No sentence claims the mechanism catches a persistent plausible error
- [ ] `CNF-99` carries the horizon-crossing-into-the-future case
- [ ] Every quoted attribution carries the cited requirement's own words — run the check by hand
      over the diff, since `tools/check_citations.py` covers the Markdown and `pv-vwe.18` is the
      bead that extends it
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes

comments.text:
Re-scoped 2026-09-21 after a three-reader panel (opus, codex gpt-6-astra, codex gpt-5.6-sol). rloop's codex Manager blocked on this ticket as originally written and was right to: its acceptance criteria demanded a trace leaving the machine unrouted while its options included withdrawing that protection.

The panel changed the answer. Verified: the horizon disjunct of LDG-16's set rule can never fire, because a backward move crossing now+interval that does not land in the past lands in the future and therefore also triggers the clear. The harm it was meant to stop is real and reachable - a poison that IS the median has zero deviation and LDG-60 cannot exclude it by construction (sources 100,100,104, one corrupted to 103, 6100 usable sats, 61s -> 59s). A second counterexample offered in the panel was directionally inverted and does not stand; this one does. Deletion rejected, universal destruction fence rejected (LDG-16's own natural-expiry sentence plus a 40% reserve cost at PRV-13e's hourly default, and LDG-65 inverts during an outage), re-keying the single column rejected (it silently deletes STO-54's restore grace). Two facts, on two clocks. ADR-0026 has the argument.

comments.author: master
comments.text:
Landed. LDG-16 owns the rule; PRV-13e, 05-persistence's machines rows, STO-49, STO-54, LDG-62,
LDG-65, OPS-41, CNF-99 and CNF-295 follow it. The two facts are machines.rate_confirmation_ref
(an STO-49 acceptance order, not an instant) and machines.destroy_not_before.

Two things ADR-0026 did not say, both found by the two-axis review, both now amendments on the ADR
as well as rules:

1. A backward move never confirms itself. The accepted discharge text - 'one that still derives
exhaustion confirms it and permits routing' - assumed an arming that was itself an exhaustion,
which the widened arming rule two sentences earlier had stopped guaranteeing. Read literally it
restores the defect the mechanism exists to stop: an ordinary wobble from two hours out to one
hour fifty arms the reference, the next reading is the poisoned one, and being strictly later it
confirms an exhaustion no observation before it derived. Discharge is now 'the first strictly later
accepted observation whose own write does not arm it again'. CNF-99 feeds that trace.

2. A move of a date that had already passed arms nothing. Without it a machine already known to be
exhausted goes back behind a fresh confirmation once per interval for as long as the rate drifts,
and LDG-13 becomes unreachable. The withdrawn rule had the same exclusion.

Also decided and added to the ADR: LDG-64's bound and the suspended tenant bypass the reference but
not the destruction deadline, which costs the bound at most one re-derivation interval and keeps
the restore grace a rule without exceptions.

Considered and kept, against review: 'acceptance order' (ADR-0026's own words; the 'order' on
CONTEXT.md's Deposit avoid-list is the provider-order sense) and destroy_not_before (states the
rule with no polarity ambiguity, unlike a second '_deadline' beside rate_outage_deadline; the
schema row now distinguishes it from destroy_committed).

Gates: nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh green, unpiped, on the committed text. Quoted
attributions checked by hand over the diff - the citations gate caught one, where two quotes shared

title: LDG-70: the cached balance and the sum, as one theorem
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`).

## What to build

`LDG-70`'s two representations of one balance, in `Provisiond.Ledger`.

`LDG-5` says "**Balance is the sum of entries** and nothing else"; `LDG-6` puts a running balance on
every entry; `STO-21` permits a cached one. `LDG-70` settles which the authorization reads: the sum
"is a definition, not a read strategy, and the read is `balance_after` on the tenant's latest
entry", written "inside the same serialized transaction that appends the entry".

`Ledger` today carries `Balances.sum : Int` and `available = sum − reserved`. It has no entry
history, no `balance_after`, and therefore no way to state the property `LDG-70` exists for: that
the cached read and the definition cannot diverge.

Model entries carrying a sequence, an amount and a `balance_after`; prove that an append preserves
the equality, that the authoritative read is `balance_after` at the greatest sequence, and that the
two disagree exactly when an append used a stale predecessor.

Every reader on the 2026-09-21 panel ranked this, and all three ranked it third.

## Why this one

This is `LDG-73`'s shape, and that shape has already cost this set once: the meter carried "what has
been charged" as a second representation until the rounding-credit redesign replaced it, and three
requirements were deleted rather than changed. The question `LDG-73` leaves standing is "whether the
second representation should exist" — the model is what answers it with a proof instead of an
argument.

## Red build

An append that computes `balance_after` from a row other than the current greatest sequence: two
credits of 10 and 7 against the same predecessor leave the latest `balance_after` at 7 while the
entries sum to 17, and a create is then authorized against a balance the sum does not fund.

## Must not touch

`Ledger.clamp` and the existing `available` definition; `LDG-35`'s serialization is already modelled
by `serializedAuthorization` and this composes with it rather than restating it. No SQL, no index
model.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Entry history with `balance_after`, and the equality theorem over append
- [ ] The authoritative read is the greatest sequence, with a witness for a non-greatest read
- [ ] The stale-predecessor witness above, refused with the guard and admitted without it
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, `ci.yml` row per new parameter,
      rehearsed locally
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes
close_reason: done

comments.author: master
comments.text: Landed by rloop Run 20260926T183014.077293953Z-2295892, Round 1. The ticket's Red build was wrong as written: "two credits of 10 and 7 against the same predecessor leave the latest balance_after at 7 while the entries sum to 17, and a create is then authorized against a balance the sum does not fund" -- two stale credits make the cache UNDER-state the sum, so every create they authorize is funded. The witness uses stale debits instead (top-up 17, two debits of 10 and 7 both computed from the 17: latest balance_after 10, sum 0, a create of 10 authorized), chosen by consultation opus+sol (B) against astra (C). The ticket's 'the two disagree exactly when an append used a stale predecessor' is false as an iff; Ledger.drift_identity states the exact difference (each append's drift is the balance_after of the row it read less the greatest row's) and divergence_names_a_stale_append the true direction (opus+sol (i), astra (ii); astra's 10/7/3 counterexample corrected the wording and is decided in drift_identity_witness). title: LDG-38's increment key and LDG-72's high-water mark
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`).

## What to build

`LDG-38`'s real increment key, and `LDG-72`'s high-water mark, in `Provisiond.Funding`.

`LDG-38`: "A `usage_debit` MUST be idempotent per **`(subject, billing period, kind, increment
end)`**." `Funding.post` writes `key := .increment w.entries.length` — the entry count, unique by
construction — so the replay that key exists to refuse cannot be expressed in the model at all.
`Funding`'s own docstring already lists "`LDG-72`'s high-water mark" among what it omits.

Give the increment its stated key, carry the high-water mark, and prove the replay refused.

## Why this one

`Provisiond.Funding` already proves exactly this property for the other money-in path:
`replay_credits_once_by_key` shows a replayed settlement crediting once under `LDG-8`'s key, and
`replay_refused_by_record` shows `STO-46`'s unique payment row catching what the key does not. The
metered path is the one that runs every interval forever, and it has neither.

## Red build

**The replay.** A worker's reply is lost; the tick recomputes the increment ending at `T` and posts
again. Under the stated key it is refused; with the key as a sequence, two `usage_debit` entries
exist for the same seconds and the rounding credit `r` has advanced twice — and `Meter`'s
`single_corruption_bound` is about a corrupt `r` in range, not about an `r` advanced by a debit that
should never have posted.

**The stale read.** `LDG-38`'s 2026-09-04 clause: a tick that reads `running` before an `LDG-74`
stop "posts an increment computed from state that is no longer true". `Fence` and `Reconcile` model
the stop; neither posts money, so nothing today connects them.

## Must not touch

`Meter.lean`'s recurrence and `Ledger.clamp`. New `Params` fields go one per line: `ci.yml`'s loop
requires exactly one red per flip.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The increment carries `(subject, billing period, kind, increment end)`, with the replay witness
      refused under it and admitted under a sequence key
- [ ] The high-water mark advances on the greatest `increment end` posted, with a witness for the
      zero-debit increment `STO-45` permits
- [ ] The stale-read trace stated, or named in the module's omissions with the reason
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, one `ci.yml` row per parameter,
      rehearsed locally
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes
close_reason: LDG-8's usage key (subject, billing period, kind, increment end) and LDG-38/LDG-72's high-water mark in Provisiond.Funding: post_replay_discarded, mark_covers_every_key, five witnesses, two ci.yml rows, each redding exactly one witness (all rows rehearsed ok by the Implementer and two Reviewers). Stale read named in the omissions with its reason. Two-axis review applied: the key-refuses-without-insert finding rejected (a unique key refuses an insert; the mark covers the rest); follow-ups pv-vwe.27, .28, .29.

title: LDG-68's period boundary, composed with the meter
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`).

## What to build

`LDG-68`'s period boundary, composed with `Provisiond.Meter`.

`LDG-68`: "**The billing period is the calendar month in UTC, and it is one boundary for the whole**"
deployment. `LDG-38` adds that "An increment also closes at every period boundary". `Meter` models
the rounding-credit recurrence and mentions the period reset in prose — "starting a period at `r =
0` posts at least what carrying a nonnegative `r` would" — but has no boundary term, so nothing
states which increments belong to which period, or that an increment straddling midnight on the
first is split rather than assigned whole.

Model the period as a key and the assignment of an increment to it; compose with the existing
recurrence rather than rewriting it.

## Red build

Carrying `r` across `00:00Z` on the first of the month; assigning a straddling increment wholly to
its closing month; or using a per-machine anniversary instead of one deployment-wide boundary — each
must fail an executable boundary witness.

## Must not touch

`Meter.postedDebit` and the corruption bound; no calendar library and no provider calendars. If a
calendar conversion cannot close on core Lean, that is the commit that names the theorem needing
Mathlib (`ADR-0025`), and it is a decision to take explicitly rather than by drift.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A period key and the assignment rule, with the three witnesses above
- [ ] The existing recurrence theorems unchanged, or the one that changes named and argued
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, `ci.yml` row per parameter, rehearsed
      locally
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes
close_reason: LDG-68's period boundary composed with Meter in the new Provisiond.Period: half-open key, split of a straddling increment (start taken as given, pv-vwe.30 named), per-period postings from r = 0, three Params fields (resetAtBoundary, splitAtBoundary, deploymentWide) each with a ci.yml row redding exactly its own witness; all 56 rows rehearsed ok. Meter, Ledger, Render untouched; Funding changed by one omission sentence. Calendar kept abstract after a Consultation (opus and sol for, astra for civil coordinates; fable out of quota). Two-axis review applied over two Rounds by opus, astra and sol: the twins named, two docstrings quoted, the finite-list omission stated. Follow-up evidence on pv-vwe.25, .28, .30.

title: The quoted-attribution gate reaches the Lean docstrings
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`).

## What to build

Extend `tools/check_citations.py`'s QUOTED rule to the docstrings under `tools/formal/`.

The gate reads root `*.md` and `docs/adr/*.md` — `docs = {f: read(f) for f in
sorted(glob.glob("*.md"))}` — and states the hole in its own docstring: "Nor a quote inside a Lean
docstring under tools/formal/: this gate reads *.md only, and a docstring quoting withdrawn wording
stayed green for a day on 2026-09-15."

There are now over ten thousand lines of Lean prose making quoted claims about requirements, and it
is the largest ungated surface in the repository by the gate's own admission.

## Why this one

The defect rate here is measured, not estimated. A throwaway script run on 2026-09-20 over the
`pv-vwe.9` diff found **twelve** quoted spans that did not appear in the requirement they were
attributed to — bold markers swallowed into a quote, a truncated amendment, and one sentence
attributed to `API-7` that is `API-40`'s. Every one passed all seven gates. The same session's brief
to a review panel carried two more, and the panel read past one of them.

This is the cheapest item on the board: no Lean, no new mechanism, one new source for a rule that
already exists and already has a failure mode the file documents.

## Shape

Extract `/-- … -/` and `/-! … -/` blocks, normalize whitespace across line wraps — the quotes wrap,
the requirements wrap, and they wrap differently — and run the existing QUOTED rule. Ratchet the
first run against a baseline the way the UNQUOTED rule is ratcheted, if the clean-tree count is not
already zero; a gate that fails a clean tree is a gate someone deletes.

## Red build

Rewrite one quoted span in a module docstring to words its requirement does not contain: the gate
exits 1 and names the file and the span. The negative control asserts the red came from this rule
and not from a missing index.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The QUOTED rule runs over `tools/formal/**/*.lean` docstrings, whitespace-normalized
- [ ] HEAD passes, or the ratchet baseline is set with the residue listed
- [ ] A `ci.yml` negative control that breaks one docstring quote and asserts the named failure
- [ ] The gate's own docstring no longer claims the hole it no longer has
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes
close_reason: done

title: SEC-46's account-status table and the release rule
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`).

## What to build

`SEC-46`'s account-status table as a total function, and the release rule as a theorem over it.

The requirement is headed "**AMENDED twice — and 'lost' turned out to mean three different things**",
and the states differ in what happens to the tenant's commitments. Release happens on one of them
and on no other.

Model the states, make the release predicate total over them with no wildcard, and prove release
holds exactly on the terminating one.

## Why this one

`SEC-39` calls confirming a termination "the largest single money movement any operator verb
performs", which is why it has its own operator ceiling. `API-63`'s own history is the warning: its
`terminated` path once released the commitments and left the meters running, and that was found by a
review pass rather than by a build. A four-state table with one releasing row is exactly the closed
space a `decide` settles and prose does not.

## Red build

An amendment that releases on `credentials_rejected`, contradicting "**Retained — losing the key is
not losing the servers**", or on `account_unreachable`, whose commitments are also retained.

## Must not touch

`API-63`'s full transaction — the meters, the affected-tenant lists and the closing debit are
`Provisiond.Fence`'s and `Provisiond.Funding`'s. This is the status table and the release predicate
over it, and nothing else.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The states as a closed enumeration with no wildcard, so a status added without a row is a red
      build
- [ ] Release holds exactly on the terminating state, decided over the whole enumeration
- [ ] Witnesses for the two retained states named above
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, `ci.yml` row if a parameter lands,
      rehearsed locally
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes
close_reason: done
