title: Model the setter: the re-derivation transition Fence has never exercised
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`). The decision is `ADR-0026`.

## What to build

The setter, in `Provisiond.Fence`. The module's own omissions say why this is owed: it excludes
"`PRV-13e`'s re-derivation, which is what sets `exhausted_since` under `LDG-16`'s horizon rule (the
column is set only in an initial world here)". **The layer models the clear and the routing and has
never exercised the rule that writes the mark**, which is why 495 tagged declarations and eleven
negative controls did not catch a branch that can never fire.

Model the re-derivation transition as a total function of the old date, the new date, the
observation consumed and the clock, carrying `ADR-0026`'s two facts as separate fields, so that a
write which both arms and clears is not representable. State the confirmation rule against the
acceptance order rather than elapsed time, and keep the two bypasses — `LDG-64`'s bound and the
suspended tenant — outside it.

## Red build

- **The dead branch, put back.** A parameter restoring the old clear-wins reading: a derivation
  moving the date from `now + 2i` to `now + i/2` leaves the machine routable before any second
  observation. Refused under `current`, admitted with the parameter off.
- **Elapsed time standing in for confirmation.** The same observation consumed twice, an interval
  apart, must not discharge the reference.
- **The restore grace discharged by an observation.** A deadline cleared by a rate that arrived
  seconds after the restore.

## Must not touch

`Provisiond.Fence`'s existing fence parameters and their witnesses — eleven `ci.yml` rows depend on
exactly one red per flip, so new fields go one per line. `Meter`'s recurrence and `Ledger`'s clamp
are out of scope.

## Blocked by

`pv-vwe.14` — the rules land first; this models what they say.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The re-derivation transition as one total function with no wildcard, both facts as separate
      fields
- [ ] The three red builds above, each with the pair the epic requires
- [ ] The existing fence theorems still hold, or the one that changes is named and argued
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, one `ci.yml` row per new parameter,
      rehearsed locally before the push
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes
close_reason: done

title: LDG-16's confirmation promise does not reach a cancellation already enqueued
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`). The rule is `LDG-16` as `ADR-0026` amended it; the
model that exhibits the gap is `Provisiond.Fence` as `pv-vwe.20` landed it (`bc08e19`).

## What the set promises, and where the promise stops

`LDG-16` opens with the promise:

> a rate-produced exhaustion MUST still be **confirmed by a strictly later accepted rate
> observation** before anything is destroyed, so a **transient** bad reading can move a date but
> cannot destroy a disk.

Its mechanism is a routing predicate, and only that:

> **The exhaustion sweep MUST route a machine where its stored `runway_until` has passed, its
> `rate_confirmation_ref` is null and its `destroy_not_before` is null or past — and MUST NOT
> route it otherwise.**

and, two sentences on:

> `OPS-41`'s re-derivation at claim is the last look before the mutation, so it reads neither
> fact except to clear them.

**Nothing gates a cancellation that is already enqueued.** `OPS-39` opens an episode "once, and
found open by every subsequent sweep until it closes", so a machine whose episode is already open
needs no second routing decision to be destroyed — and the reference is only ever read by the
routing decision.

## The trace, executed in the committed model

From `Provisiond.Witnesses.staleDateWorld` (commitment 100, stored date 0, `now` 0, one satoshi
per second, both facts null), under `Fence.current`:

```
sweep                      -- the stale stored date routes: natural expiry, reference null.
                           -- Episode 1 opens `attempting` with its attempt queued.
rederive 100 (some 5)      -- the interval's derivation writes the true date, 100.
                           -- Arms nothing: the old date had already passed. Reference null.
rateRestored 200           -- the price moves adversely, 1 -> 200 satoshis per second.
rederive 0 (some 7)        -- observation 7 moves 100 -> 0, a backward move of a date that
                           -- stood in the future: the reference arms with 7.
claim, fenceTxn, fenceWrite-- the queued attempt claims. OPS-41 re-derives at the same 200,
                           -- reads the machine unfunded, and writes the fence.
providerDelete true …      -- the disk is destroyed. `rate_confirmation_ref` is still `some 7`.
```

`#eval` on the committed tree returns `rateConfirmationRef = some 7` and `destroyed = true`.
No extension is involved, no bypass applies — the episode's one reason is `exhausted` — and
exactly one accepted observation stands behind the destruction. That is what the promise says
cannot happen.

The same shape is reachable through `LDG-62`: an extension clears both facts and writes a future
date but closes no episode, so its machine's queued attempt survives to be claimed after the next
backward derivation arms the reference (also executed: `sweep, extend 100, rateLost,
rateRestored 200, rederive 0 (some 7), claim, fenceTxn, fenceWrite, providerDelete` destroys).

## The two readings

**(a) The reference gates routing, and nothing else.** Then the promise sentence over-claims for
the second time — it was already narrowed on 2026-09-21 for the persistent plausible error — and
should be narrowed again: confirmation protects a machine the sweep would *newly* route, and not
one whose cancellation is already open. The model as committed is correct; what is owed is the
narrowing, a `CNF-99` case recording the bound, and probably a line in `11-open-findings.md`.

**(b) The promise governs.** Then something must hold the worker, and every candidate costs a
sentence somewhere else:

- `OPS-41`'s re-check reads the reference — which contradicts "it reads neither fact except to
  clear them", and has to distinguish the two cancellations `LDG-16` says are "never gated on
  the reference" (`LDG-64`'s bound, the suspended tenant) from the exhaustion it must gate;
- or the arming write invalidates the pending attempt — a new duty on `PRV-13e`'s re-derivation,
  reaching `OPS-39`'s episode and `OPS-48`'s table, on a machine whose episode may be `stalled`
  with a retry admissible;
- or the provider call refuses while the reference is armed, where `pv-vwe.20` already put the
  destruction deadline's check — but `OPS-41`'s 2026-09-09 scope refuses scoping by reason
  ("**any** exposure-reducing cancellation"), and the two bypasses are reasons.

## What is not in question

The setter `pv-vwe.20` built is faithful either way: arming, discharge by acceptance order, the
deadline and the routing predicate are `LDG-16`'s own sentences. What changes between the two
readings is whether anything on the worker's path reads the reference.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The owner picks a reading, and `ADR-0026` records it with the argument
- [ ] `LDG-16` carries it — either the narrowed promise, or the new gate and the sentence it
      amends, with the two bypasses preserved either way
- [ ] `CNF-99` feeds the trace above, whichever way it is answered
- [ ] The formal layer follows: a theorem or a negative control for the chosen reading, on the
      model `pv-vwe.20` landed
close_reason: dissolved by ADR-0027: the rate is a window median, so the trace cannot be built

title: The setter put LDG-16's deadline in a second home: the provider call, the restore formula, agedWorld
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`). Raised by the two-axis review of `bc08e19`
(`pv-vwe.20`'s setter), 2026-09-22. This is a decision, not a defect to fix blind: the same
shape as `pv-vwe.21`, and it touches the same sentence.

## What was found

Modelling the setter put `LDG-16`'s destruction deadline in a **second normative home**, and one
of `STO-54`'s formulas in two Lean modules. Three sites, in descending order of consequence.

### 1. The deadline moved into the provider call

`Provisiond.Fence.providerDelete` is tagged `@[req "OPS-41"]`. `bc08e19` wraps its fenced branch:

```lean
| .fenced n =>
  if w.deadlinePassed then
    { w with m := { w.m with destroyed := w.m.destroyed || applied }, phase := .dispatched n reply }
  else w
```

and adds `provider_waits_for_deadline`, tagged `@[req "LDG-16"]`, beside it.

`LDG-16` states the deadline as part of the sweep's routing predicate — "The exhaustion sweep MUST
route a machine where its stored `runway_until` has passed, its `rate_confirmation_ref` is null and
its `destroy_not_before` is null or past — and MUST NOT route it otherwise" — and says of the
re-derivation at claim that it "reads neither fact except to clear them". The new gate therefore

- puts an `LDG-16` rule inside an `OPS-41` declaration, which is the second-normative-copy shape
  `AGENTS.md` names ("One rule, one home; everywhere else points at it");
- gates the ordinary sweep path too, not only the two bypasses the docstring cites;
- makes a fenced worker whose deadline is still future a **silent no-op**: `else w` returns the
  world unchanged, so the attempt stays `.fenced` with nothing to advance it;
- rewrites two existing `OPS-42` proofs, `destroyed_only_by_provider_from_fenced` and
  `fenced_waits_for_the_provider`.

It also cuts against `pv-vwe.21`: there the deadline is what a worker re-reads and the reference is
what nothing on its path reads. Settle `pv-vwe.21` first or together, not separately.

### 2. `STO-54`'s restore formula has two homes

`Restore.World` gains `interval`, `boot` takes it as a fourth argument, and
`restore_writes_deadline` proves the deadline is `t.now + t.interval` under `STO-54`'s "the restore
instant plus one re-derivation interval". `Fence.restoreGrace` computes
`some (restoreInstant + w.interval)` for the same sentence. Two modules, one formula.

`pv-vwe.20` owed `Restore.lean` a re-quoting only; the `interval` field, `boot`'s arity and the new
theorem are beyond it. They may well be right — decide whether the formula's home is `Restore` with
`Fence` pointing at it, or the reverse.

### 3. `agedWorld` changed shape, not just its fields

The fixture had to lose `exhaustedSince` with the column. It also gained `enqueue … .exhausted`,
which is a different world, not a renamed one. Lowest stakes of the three; confirm the witness
still traps what it trapped.

## The decision

For each site: keep it and name the rule's one home (amending the requirement that loses it), or
revert it to what `pv-vwe.20` actually asked for. `ADR-0026` is the precedent for writing the
answer down rather than leaving it in the model.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of the three sites resolved: kept with its home named, or reverted
- [ ] If `providerDelete`'s gate is kept, the forever-`.fenced` world is either shown unreachable
      or given the event that clears it, with a witness
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, unpiped
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes

comments.author: master
comments.text:
Decided 2026-09-23, with ADR-0027, and this ticket shrinks.

Site 1 -- providerDelete's deadline gate -- was not a second home. LDG-16 says the re-check "reads
neither fact except to clear them", says of the two bypasses "Neither reaches the predicate above",
and says of the same two "Both do respect the destruction deadline". The three cannot all hold: if
the bypasses never reach the sweep's predicate and must respect the deadline, the worker's path
reads the deadline. The gate is the resolution, and ADR-0027 admits it into LDG-16's text. This
ticket's first site is withdrawn as a finding; the reference half of the question is moot, since
the reference itself is withdrawn.

Site 2 -- STO-54's restore formula in both Restore and Fence -- decided: a small dedicated module
that exists for that one formula, which both import. Not Tables or Claim, which own other things;
placing it there for import convenience was the wrong reason.

Site 3 -- agedWorld's shape -- confirm the witness still traps what it trapped, when the formal

title: The Lean quoted-attribution gate reaches 4% of the quotes, and pv-vwe.18's twelve do not reconcile
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe` — the formal layer (`ADR-0025`). Raised by the two-axis review of `cd76988`
(`pv-vwe.18`), 2026-09-22. `pv-vwe.18`'s three acceptance criteria are met as written; what is not
met is the justification the bead argued them from.

## What was measured

`pv-vwe.18` extended the `QUOTED` rule over Lean docstrings. The rule fires only where `ATTRIB`
matches — a speech verb, or `` `X`'s <noun> that ``, in the same `SPLIT` chunk as the quote.

- **30 of the 751 quotes of four words or more in Lean docstrings reach the check**, because only
  33 of 1713 chunks carry an attribution. That is 4% of what the bead called "the largest ungated
  surface in the repository".
- **Demonstrated, not inferred.** In a throwaway copy, `Admission.lean:30`'s
  `` `API-7`'s headline — "**Authentication MUST happen before request-body validation.**" `` was
  rewritten to `"**Authentication MUST happen after the body is parsed and validated.**"`, words
  that appear nowhere in `04-api-contract.md`. `python3 tools/check_citations.py` exits **0**. The
  sentence carries no speech verb, so `ATTRIB` never matches it.

## The bead's own evidence does not reconcile

`pv-vwe.18` justified itself with "a throwaway script run on 2026-09-20 over the `pv-vwe.9` diff
found **twelve** quoted spans that did not appear in the requirement they were attributed to".

- The `pv-vwe.9` tree (`3e28ce7`) was restored, Markdown and Lean, and the new gate run over it:
  **three findings, the same three false positives baselined today. Zero of the twelve.**
- One of the twelve was named in the bead: "one sentence attributed to `API-7` that is `API-40`'s".
  `git log -S` finds it unchanged since `3e28ce7`. The sentence reads
  `` `API-40` … and it says "`API-7`'s ordering applies to authenticated endpoints" ``, and that
  phrase **is** in `API-40`'s body. The prose is correct. The throwaway script blamed `API-7`
  because `API-7` sits inside the quote — the inverted attribution `find()`'s own comment rejects.
  So the headline example was itself a false positive of the script, not a defect in the repo.
- A second class the bead named, "bold markers swallowed into a quote", is unreachable **by
  construction**: `norm()` does `re.sub(r"[*`~]", "", s)`, stripping exactly those markers from
  both sides before comparison.

The honest reading is that the twelve were mostly the script's false positives, and that the
measured defect rate which justified this ticket is unestablished. That does not make the gate
worthless — it closed a real hole, and `1a2af47` and `b373fa8` fixed seven genuine stale docstring
claims by hand in the same session — but it does mean the next decision should not be taken on the
strength of "twelve".

## The decision

Widening `ATTRIB` so a quote needs no speech verb is not a Lean-only change: `ATTRIB` is the
pre-existing rule and the same widening applies to every `*.md` in the repository, where it would
surface an unknown number of findings and would have to be ratcheted. That is a change to a rule
this set already owns, so it is `ADR`-shaped rather than an implementation detail. The alternatives:

1. **Widen `ATTRIB`** — a quote adjacent to a citation is attributed, verb or no verb. Measure the
   Markdown blast radius first; the baseline grows by whatever it finds.
2. **A Lean-only ATTRIB** — docstrings are prose written to explain one declaration, so a quote
   near a citation there is likelier to be an attribution than in requirement prose. Costs a second
   rule with a scope condition, which `AGENTS.md`'s "one rule, one home" argues against.
3. **Accept 4% and say so.** Narrow the gate's own docstring claim from the surface it reads to the
   quotes it can actually check, so no later reader takes green as evidence the docstrings are
   clean. Cheapest, and honest, but leaves the hole `pv-vwe.18` was opened to close.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The chosen option decided with its measurement, not its estimate — for (1), the Markdown
      finding count measured before the rule changes
- [ ] Whatever is chosen, `check_citations.py`'s module docstring states the reach the gate
      actually has, since it is the file's own record of what it does and does not cover
- [ ] A red build for the newly-covered shape, if the reach widens
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, unpiped
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff applied before the ticket closes
close_reason: Done in ef16d1a; see the closing comment

comments.author: master
comments.text: Further evidence from pv-vwe.17's Round-2 review (2026-09-26): corrupting each of the 23 docstring quotes in the new tools/formal/Provisiond/Period.lean in turn produced zero check_citations findings. The module's house style (`LDG-38`'s split, "..."; `LDG-68`: "...") matches neither ATTRIB branch. The quotes were verified verbatim by hand and by the gate's own norm() driven directly, so the work is sound; what the gate does not see there is what this ticket measures.

comments.author: master
comments.text:
Measurement for option 1, taken 2026-09-27 at `1cbe4ba`, read-only (a scratch script importing
`check_citations.py`'s own SPLIT, QUOTE, HISTORICAL, TEACHING, norm and pool logic; only the
attribution step changed). The widened rule tested: a quote of four words or more is attributed to
the **nearest citation before it in the same chunk**, verb or no verb.

| Corpus | current rule, findings | widened rule, quotes checked | widened rule, findings |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Markdown (`*.md` at the root) | 0 | 194 | 50 |
| Lean docstrings | 3 (baselined) | 598 | 62 |

Markdown findings by file: `11-open-findings.md` 22, `impl-report-01.md` 5, then 4 or fewer each
across ten documents.

**Precision is low.** A sample of seven Markdown findings, each read in its sentence, and eleven
Lean findings, every sixth, judged from the quote and the id it was attributed to rather than read
in full:

- **Real, one:** `03-operation-lifecycle.md:774` and `:913-914` put "what makes `OPS-33`'s early
  release safe" in quote marks as `OPS-36`'s words. `OPS-36` says "**This is the branch that makes
  `OPS-33`'s early release safe**" (`:553-554`, unchanged since `56a7d56`); the quoted form was
  written by `660cd59` (2026-08-31) and was never verbatim. `:913` also says `OPS-36` "called
  `OPS-41`" that, where `OPS-36` calls its own survival branch that. The current gate misses it
  because "calls" is not in `SPEECH`.
- **Wrong owner** (most of the rest): the nearest citation is not the quote's source — "`STO-43`
  had even written down why … a citation to `STO-14` "is not a clock"" blames `STO-14`;
  `Admission.lean`'s `API-24` sentence quoting "`kind` MUST come from the closed set in `DOM-17`"
  and then "Handlers MUST NOT choose …" blames `DOM-17` for the second.
- **Not a quotation**: scare quotes and paraphrased meanings — "the tenant has replied", "we have
  no record", "already deferred, or already claimed again".
- **A document, not a requirement**: "this document already concedes the limiter is "trivially
  defeated by distributed sources"" blames `API-34`.
- **Historical wording `HISTORICAL` does not recognise**: `AccountStatus.lean`'s "the rule before
  it, `SEC-46`'s "When a provider account is lost …"".

So option 1 as "nearest citation" would add 112 baseline entries. Of the eighteen sampled, one is
confirmed real; the precision estimate is rough, and low. It is not a ratchet anyone could read. A usable widening needs a better attribution
step than proximity, for example the possessive `` `X`'s "…" `` and `` `X`: "…" `` shapes plus
"calls" in `SPEECH`, measured the same way before choosing. Option 3 (state the 4% reach in the
gate's docstring) stays the honest floor whatever is chosen.

To reproduce: import `check_citations`, and for each SPLIT chunk not matched by HISTORICAL or
TEACHING, attribute each QUOTE of four or more normalised words to the last `` `NS-n` `` citation
that starts before it, then apply `find()`'s pool and fragment match unchanged.

comments.author: master
comments.text: Decided 2026-10-01 by the owner (panel 2026-09-27 rejected proximity unanimously): an owner-free check that every quote of four or more words in a Lean docstring appears somewhere in the requirements or ADRs (opus measured 19 of 761 flagged at 5cbe244); check_citations.py's docstring states the gate's real reach (about 53 of 816 Lean quotes under ATTRIB at HEAD); and the pool stops letting any ADR's text satisfy a quote attributed to a requirement (astra). Explicit attribution syntax across Markdown and Lean is the later direction if verbatim-but-misattributed quotes start to matter. 'calls' stays out of SPEECH (a summary verb by design); if added, only to a quote-only set like CONSULTS.

comments.text: Done 2026-10-02 in ef16d1a (rloop Run 20261002T205047, two Rounds, four-Reviewer Panel each). Measured at c5e31be: 925 Lean docstring quotes of 4+ words, 56 compared under QUOTED (not the bead's 30 of 751 nor the decision's 53 of 816); 16 absent from the root documents plus ADRs, of which 7 differed only in nested quote marks, 3 sat in HISTORICAL chunks, 5 remained: one real misquote (Claim.lean 'advance[s]', STO-3 says 'advance') fixed; two QUOTE pairing artefacts (Rescue, Wire) and one HISTORICAL miss (AccountStatus) reworded; Witnesses.lean's quotation of Lean's own 'proved that the proposition' baselined with its reason. title: LDG-38 says the key protects exact replays; a replay that rounds or clamps to nothing escapes it
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe`. Raised by `pv-vwe.16`'s Implementer and by two of its Panel's Reviewers (astra, sol), 2026-09-26.

## What the model shows

`LDG-38` (`12-billing-and-ledger.md`, the high-water paragraph) gives the mark's reason as "without the mark the
deduplication key protects only exact replays, not overlapping ones". That is too generous to the key. `LDG-8`'s key sits on
the entry, and a conflict is a refused insert. An exact replay whose recomputed debit rounds or clamps to nothing inserts no
row (`STO-45`'s "transaction with no ledger entry"), so nothing conflicts, yet `r` moves and, where it clamped, a second
`STO-37` deficiency is booked. Evaluated in `Provisiond.Funding` with `markDiscards := false`:

- `[post 1 (1/2), post 1 (1/2)]` leaves one entry of −1, as the key promises, but moves `r` from 1/2 to 0.
- With 1 sat of commitment left, `[post 7 (7/5), post 7 (7/5)]` books a second deficiency of 1 and moves `r` from 3/5 to 1/5.

Under `Funding.current` the mark refuses all of these (`post_replay_discarded`). So the specified system's behaviour is not in
question; only the sentence's account of what each guard buys is.

## Also

- `Provisiond.Witnesses.remeter_charged_without_the_mark` quotes that sentence over a trace whose first half is an *exact*
  replay the key admits. The quote is verbatim, but its re-meter half is the only part it supports.
- The Panel read `pv-vwe.16`'s brief ("A key collision refuses the whole increment") as requiring the key to refuse whenever it
  is already held, even with no insert. The Manager rejected that: it models a pre-check the specification does not require,
  and a deployment's unique index behaves the way the model does.

## Decide

Whether to amend `LDG-38`'s sentence, for example to "the key protects only replays that write an entry", with a dated note
after the record. Then align the witness's docstring.
close_reason: LDG-38 and LDG-8 say what the key stops (an insert, where the first posting left a key) and that the mark and the start rule stop every replay; STO-45 says a discarded increment moves nothing; CNF-160 carries the case; the witnesses' docstrings moved with the sentences.

comments.author: master
comments.text:
Corrections from the Spec axis of the two-axis review of `f166a01` (2026-09-26), checked by `#eval`:

1. **The example wording above is false.** "The key protects only replays that write an entry" does
   not hold: in `remeterTrace` with `discardOff`, the replay of `post 9 (2/5)` DOES write an entry
   (−1 under key k9) and the key does not stop it, because the ORIGINAL posting wrote none. The
   accurate form is "only replays of an increment whose first posting wrote an entry".
2. **`LDG-8` makes the same over-claim, and this ticket names only `LDG-38`.** `LDG-8`'s "derives the
   *same* key and conflicts" (12-billing-and-ledger.md ~127–128) is the sentence
   `increment_replay_refused_by_key` quotes. Any amendment covers both sentences, each with its
   dated note after the record.
3. **`STO-45` leaves the discarded increment implicit.** Its "Every increment updates it" reads as
   universal and does not carve out an increment `LDG-38` discards. The model treats a discard as
   moving nothing, the only reading consistent with "discarded, not posted", but the text never
   says so. Same family; decide it with this one.

Under the rules as they stand the behaviour is not in question: the high-water mark refuses these
replays (`post_replay_discarded`), and under `current` an increment end never posts twice. This is
a wording decision about what the key alone promises.

comments.author: master
comments.text: Decided 2026-10-02 by the owner: say what each one protects. With pv-vwe.30's start rule (an increment starts at the subject's latest high-water mark), the mark and the start rule stop every replay, exact or overlapping; the idempotency key is a backstop only for replays of an increment whose first posting wrote an entry. Amend LDG-38's 'without the mark the deduplication key protects only exact replays, not overlapping ones' and LDG-8's 'derives the *same* key and conflicts', each with its dated note, and STO-45 states that a discarded increment moves nothing. Rejected: a zero-amount entry per increment so the key sees every replay (a row per tick; contradicts LDG-72's 'a mark ahead of every entry is ordinary'). Land with pv-vwe.30: both edit LDG-38.

title: ADR-0025 says rational witnesses close by decide +kernel; two ci.yml row witnesses cannot
description:
## Parent

`pv-vwe`. Raised by `pv-vwe.16`'s Implementer, 2026-09-26.

## The conflict

title: Wire canonicalization and redaction
description:
## Parent

pv-vwe — the formal layer, M2 through M8 (`ADR-0025`).

## What to build

`API-12`'s canonical serialization and the fingerprint preimage as functions; `API-21`/`STO-50`'s projections from internal records into public views as explicit functions, so a new internal field cannot leak through generic serialization; `SEC-8`'s foreign-and-absent indistinguishability as a theorem on observable responses. Lean knows nothing about HTTP; parser and transport correspondence is a named assumption.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Canonicalization idempotent and key-order insensitive, proved
- [ ] Fingerprint preimage includes the endpoint, decided on the request-target construction

- [ ] `SEC-8`: equal observable responses for an absent and a foreign-owned machine
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, and every new check's CI negative control asserts the red came from that check.
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff (standards against `AGENTS.md`/`ADR-0025`/the glossary, spec against the cited requirement sentences) applied before the next ticket starts.

## Blocked by

- None (can start immediately)

title: LDG-38 places an increment's start only after a rate-change split, so a re-meter spanning the mark charges seconds twice
description:
Raised by the Spec axis of the two-axis review of `f166a01` (`pv-vwe.16`), 2026-09-26, from the model.

## What was found

`LDG-38` discards an increment "at or before" the high-water mark, keyed on the increment's **end**.
Nothing in the set states where an increment **starts**. So a re-meter that re-observes seconds the
mark already covers, in one increment ending after the mark, is admitted whole.

Trace under `Funding.current`, every rule on: `[post 7 (7/5), post 10 2]`, where the second posting
is a re-meter re-observing seconds 0–10. The mark is 7, the second increment ends at 10, so it is
neither discarded by the mark nor refused by the key (k10 is new), and it posts −2 under k10.
Seconds 0–7 are charged twice.

`lean-01.md` (~170–174) asked for exactly this: an increment's start as well as its end. The
model's omission list (`Funding.lean` ~72–93) does not name increment starts either.

## Why it is filed rather than fixed

The repair is a requirement's: either `LDG-38` states that an increment starts at the mark (or at
the previous increment's end) and clips the charge to it, or the key carries the start, or the text
argues why a re-observation spanning the mark cannot arise. That choice is the owner's.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `LDG-38` (or its owner) says where an increment starts, or says in its own text why an
      increment spanning the mark cannot be posted, with the argument and not an assertion
- [ ] `Provisiond.Funding` models the start, or names it in the omissions with the reason
close_reason: LDG-38 carries the seed and the start rule (an increment starts at the subject's latest high-water mark, split at every period boundary and rate change; a re-meter overlapping the mark is clipped); LDG-72 says how the latest mark is read; CNF-304, CNF-305; Provisiond.Funding models the start (startsAtMark) and the seed (seedOnBillable), no_second_charged_twice is the theorem, each with a ci.yml row.

title: Only API-63 closes an increment when a subject stops billing; an ordinary stop never charges the last partial interval
description:
Raised by all four readers of the 2026-10-02 panel on `pv-vwe.30` (fable, opus, astra, sol), each
independently. Pre-existing; separate from where an increment starts.

## What was found

Only `API-63` requires a closing increment when a subject stops billing: "post each subject's
closing partial increment against its commitment (`LDG-38`), for the time between its last increment
end and the recording instant" (`04-api-contract.md` ~1251–1252), and only for an account recorded
`terminated`. An ordinary stop — `LDG-74`'s gone observation, a successful delete — has no such
rule; `LDG-32`'s "the machine stops billing" is a precondition, not a posting rule. So a subject
billable for less than one meter interval (`LDG-37`: "at least one transaction per billable subject
per interval") is never charged, and every subject's last partial interval is charged only if a tick
happens to land between its last increment end and its stop. `API-63` itself notes that a debit
after release can be clamped away entirely ("the customer's last minutes would be free").

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `LDG-38` (or `LDG-74`) requires the write that stops a subject's meter to post the closing
      increment from the subject's latest mark to the stop instant, in the same transaction and
      before any commitment release, as `API-63` does for termination
- [ ] A `CNF` case: a machine billable for less than one interval is charged for its billable
      seconds
close_reason: Accepted after Round 2 review. title: QUOTE mispairs after an unpaired mark: a quotation SPLIT cuts, or a quoted span under 8 characters, hides the quotes after it from every rule
description:
Found by the opus Reviewer of the pv-vwe.25 Run, 2026-10-02, and verified by mutation.

tools/check_citations.py's SPLIT is `(?<=[.!?])\s+|...`. It breaks on a sentence ender followed by whitespace inside a quotation as readily as outside it, so a two-sentence quotation, or a `... ` elision with a space after the period, is cut in two chunks each holding an unpaired quote mark; QUOTE matches neither half and the span is counted by no rule. Corrupting Fence.lean:168's `OPS-41` quote "keyed on the tenant's current state ... and not on the episode's \`reasons\` set" to "current posture" exits 0 with the printed quote count unchanged. `…` (U+2026) and `...,` reach fragments() and are checked.

Measured on the tree at the Run's close: 32 chunks carry an odd number of straight quote marks, about 16 spans across eight files (Fence 10, Tables 8, Wire 4, Admission, Claim, Rehost, Restore, Witnesses 2 each). The module docstring names the limit under "What it cannot see" for both rules.

Changing SPLIT changes QUOTED's reach over Markdown and Lean alike, so it is a measured decision: count the Markdown and Lean findings a quote-aware splitter (one that does not cut inside a paired quotation) surfaces before choosing. Alternative: reword the standing spans so the elision carries no trailing whitespace, which fixes the inventory and not the hole.

Acceptance:
- [ ] Either SPLIT no longer cuts inside a paired quotation, with the Markdown and Lean finding counts measured before the change and the residue disposed of (misquotes fixed, the rest baselined with a reason), or the decision not to is recorded with that measurement
- [ ] If changed: a ci.yml negative control that corrupts a two-sentence or spaced-elision quotation and asserts the named finding
- [ ] nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh green, unpiped
close_reason: Implemented and validated in c834a1d; measurement and acceptance evidence in comments

title: Concurrent gate runs can expose a truncated formal index to citation and region checks
description:
## Observed failure

During the independent Round-1 review of pv-gip.21 at 8cf2253, Opus's first full gate failed in citations and regions with JSONDecodeError while the same unmodified source passed on rerun. The retained log is /var/tmp/review-3453423-gates-final.log. It reports:

- lake build completed successfully;
- lake exe gate reported 720 tagged declarations and no axiom-policy violations;
- the immediately following wrapper count saw only 42 index lines;
- both consumers failed in check_citations.read_index at json.loads, with "Expecting value: line 1 column 1".

The panel report is .rloop/runs/20261005T142936.630893945Z-3453423/feedback-1-opus.md. It also reports a NUL-filled head in the index, consistent with overlapping truncating writers. The Manager directly checked the retained traceback/count log and the wrapper/consumer source; the particular competing process was not identified. A later complete gate on this same revision passed, as did the Manager's independent gate.

## Source of the race

Current tools/check_formal.sh writes shared build artifacts directly:

    lake exe gate > .lake/index.jsonl
    lake exe render > .lake/regions.jsonl

There is no publication/reader coordination around these writes. check-all.sh orders generation before consumers within one invocation, but a second invocation in the same working tree can truncate the same files while the first reads them. tools/check_citations.py read_index and tools/check_regions.py load_formal consume those paths directly.

The index failure was observed. The regions publication path has the same shape but was not separately reproduced. This is an existing gate failure on unrelated shared output, not a defect in CNF-99 and not a reason to reopen pv-gip.21. It meets the follow-up criterion of a check failing for the wrong reason.

## Required outcome and verification

Ensure overlapping gate invocations on an unchanged working tree cannot expose partially published index/region output to their consumers. Preserve the existing fail-closed handling of generation failure, missing toolchains and invalid formal content; do not turn read failures into skips or certify stale output from a failed generation. Implementation mechanism is deliberately left undecided.

Add a reproducible overlap/interleaving regression that fails under the current publication path for the intended reason and passes with the repair, and exercise generation-failure behavior. Re-run the affected ci.yml negative controls in place with restoration between mutations and the required unpiped full gate. Avoid concurrent tracked-source mutations: this issue concerns competing artifact publication on identical source, not coordinating different edits to one tree.

No specification policy change is requested. Priority is low because serial gate runs pass; the issue affects parallel readers sharing a checkout.

title: Fence core: both commit orderings of OPS-42
description:
## Parent

pv-vwe — the formal layer, M2 through M8 (`ADR-0025`).

## What to build

The cancellation fence composed on the claim model. Model state: the machine's commitment, stored `runway_until`, the fence as an optional episode id; events: sweep routing on the stored date, claim, the fence transaction with its funding re-check inside it as a Bool parameter, extension in its own serialization guarded on the fence, provider delete outside the serialization, reply, settlement. `OPS-42`: 'The cancellation and the extension MUST contend for one row, so that one of them provably loses'.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Extension first: the re-check reads the grown commitment and the worker makes no provider call
- [ ] Fence first: the extension is refused, opening no commitment and moving no balance
- [ ] Destruction only after a fence transaction whose re-check read unfunded
- [ ] Witness: re-check outside the fence transaction admits the paid-machine deletion
- [ ] Witness: the fence holding the attempt id refuses a legitimate retry
- [ ] A successful cancellation witness and a successful extension witness
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, and every new check's CI negative control asserts the red came from that check.
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff (standards against `AGENTS.md`/`ADR-0025`/the glossary, spec against the cited requirement sentences) applied before the next ticket starts.

- pv-vwe.1
close_reason: Fence core landed: Provisiond/Fence.lean, six witnesses, two CI controls; check-all green

comments.author: master
comments.text:
Reading choices the Markdown leaves open, recorded at close (2026-09-16):
1. The lost-race abort ('another actor won') settles as the same terminal transaction as the funded abort and writes the re-derived runway_until; OPS-41 conditions that write on the funded case, OPS-42 says only 'settle as OPS-41 requires'. On a machine read unfunded the stored date it writes is no later than the one it had.
2. 'Destruction only after a fence transaction whose re-check read unfunded' lands as three step-level theorems (destroyed_only_by_provider_from_fenced, fenced_only_by_fence_txn, fenced_waits_for_the_provider) chained by docstring, not one invariant over reachable worlds; pv-vwe.10's 'over all reachable states' criterion is where a Reachable predicate belongs.
3. The sweep routes nothing while an episode is open; joining an open episode (OPS-39) is pv-vwe.10's.
4. Every witness trace carries the split variant's fenceWrite step, inert under current, so one schedule runs both designs and the CI control turns exactly one witness red.
Two-axis review applied: writeDate flag removed from finish (pv-vwe.10's parameter, added early); omissions paragraph extended (abort predicate, date writes, retry-from-stalled, fence-names-open-episode, LDG-62 sizing, resolved_at); LDG-69/OPS-39/LDG-10 assertions turned into quotes; retry docstring re-attributed to OPS-48's row.

title: Reconciliation knowledge

title: OPS-11 install row: should a deterministic caller error past a bytes-on-disk marker be failed?
description: Surfaced by the 2026-09-14 three-reviewer check of pv-vwe.2. OPS-11's install row sends the deterministic caller errors (invalid_request, not_found, unsupported, authentication, rate_limited) to failed even after OPS-45's write-started marker is set. On rootfs_via_rescue and raw_disk the marker means bytes reached the disk, and WIR-35/OPS-31 say recording such an install as if nothing happened 'tells a caller its data survived'. On provider_native/provider_catalogue the marker means dispatch only, where a 4xx after dispatch is honestly failed. Decide whether the row should distinguish the two marker meanings (n_r past a bytes-on-disk marker for every kind) or stand. The Lean (tools/formal/Provisiond/Tables.lean, installRow) follows the row as written; a decision changes one arm and the row together.
close_reason: done

comments.author: master
comments.text: Three-reader panel 2026-09-15 (fresh Fable, codex gpt-6-astra xhigh, codex gpt-5.6-sol xhigh; brief and answers in .context/pv-x8r-*.md, gitignored). All three: the row STANDS. The story is reachable only on rootfs_via_rescue and only as the rescue engine's own kind choice (PRV-5 never touches the installer). needs_reconciliation is defined as 'outcome unknown' and here it is known; the operator's only verb would be abandoned -> failed anyway. Observation 2 is not a contradiction: not_applied is a positive assertion in resolution, the classifier's failed asserts only 'did not complete, outcome known' - the set already writes failed on a bytes-on-disk disk via abandoned. The defect is DISCLOSURE: the caller cannot tell an untouched-disk failed from a partitioned one. Owner decision: adopt sol's shape - OPS-3 defines failed weakly; OPS-11 install row gains the sentence; WIR-9a requires details.disk_effect (none|destructive_boundary_crossed|unknown) on install errors; OPS-45's 'bytes reached the disk' softened to what a before-the-phase marker proves; API-51 'second purchase' scoped to creates; OPS-31's 'tells a caller its data survived' replaced (the caller never sees a verb); retryable per DOM-17 (NOT true); Lean unchanged except a theorem pinning the arm; glossary gains marker, evidence, disk effect. Rejected: n_r for every kind (b), driver prohibition (c), trap-only (d), Fable's view boolean (covers no dispatch case), astra's extras (resolution/install_strategy on the view, PRV-5 nonzero-exit clause) - not needed for this decision.
